# Road to production and higher classification

This page lists every known gap and open condition: what is still to do before live use, and what changes as your organization moves to a higher classification level. It is one list, kept in the gap register, so nothing found during planning or building is lost.

Each item is listed once, at the lowest level where it matters. It still matters at every level above that. Items for exchange with allies are listed on their own, because that work can start at any level.

Production means live use for real work at your organization's site. An item that blocks production must be closed, or accepted by your organization's authorizing official, before that. An item that does not block production still matters at its level. Where the right level or the effect on production was not clear, the register uses the stricter value. Of the 490 items, 426 block production.

This page shows the register, not progress. Some items may already be closed by evidence. The [gaps page](../accreditation/gaps.mdx) shows the current state of each one. Your organization decides what it accepts.

## How this list stays current

The list is generated from the gap register, [`compliance/gaps.json`](https://github.com/VitalPointAI/near-ai-vscode/blob/main/compliance/gaps.json), and its POA&M items. The same register feeds the POA&M, the accreditation pages and the assessor package. Each item names the lowest level where it matters (`appliesAt`) and whether it blocks production (`blocksProduction`); an item without both is refused. Any open condition found while planning or building a phase is added to the register before the phase closes, and the phase summary cites its id. CI fails when this page differs from the register, or when a phase summary lists an open condition without a gap id.

## Now, at every level {#now}

These matter today, at every level, including unclassified work.

### Blocks production {#now-blocks}

- **G1. Incident response and advisory operation still need evidence.** Keep the published incident response plan and supported versions policy current. Record a product response exercise and evidence of advisory and notification procedures. Your organization approves, exercises, and records its own deployment response. Controls: IR-1, IR-4, IR-6, IR-8, SI-5. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 44.1.
- **G2. Gate decision records are not tamper-evident and cannot be exported.** Write decision records through one record writer into a hash-chained local audit with signed heads, then add a command that exports them for assessors. Controls: AU-4, AU-6, AU-9, AU-10. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g02; first milestone: Record writer and hash-chained local audit with signed heads (Phase 32.1).
- **G3. The messaging relay has no inbound authentication yet.** Authenticate every inbound request to the relay and allow only listed senders and channels, as planned for the relay. Controls: AC-17, IA-2, IA-9, SC-23. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g03; first milestone: Inbound authenticity, allowlisting and channel manifests for the relay (Phase 75).
- **G4. No build provenance or attestation for the VSIX, the relay image or the package.** Attest the release artifacts with GitHub artifact attestations in the Release workflow, and verify them when the dashboard data is refreshed. Controls: SR-4, SR-11, SI-7, CM-14. Owner role: release-owner. Planned in Phase 44.
- **G5. No vulnerability scan or SBOM for the relay container image.** Build an SBOM of the relay image and scan it with a pinned, checksummed scanner, reporting high and critical findings. Controls: RA-5, CM-8, SR-4. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 44.
- **G6. No static analysis of the source code.** Run static analysis on every pull request and on main, and keep its results as evidence. Controls: SA-11(1). Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 44.
- **G7. No CODEOWNERS file; review routing is by convention.** Add a CODEOWNERS file that names the owner for the gate paths and the compliance sources. Controls: CM-5, AC-5. Owner role: owner. Planned in Phase 44.
- **G8. No backup and recovery guidance for the messaging relay.** The hub's backup, restore and restore drill are documented; the relay's operator runbook adds its backups, restore and upgrades. Controls: CP-9, CP-10. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g08; first milestone: Relay operator runbook with backup, restore and upgrade steps (Phase 84).
- **G9. No standalone threat model or data-flow diagram.** Publish one threat model and a data-flow diagram per component, each reviewed at least once a year. Controls: RA-3, PL-8, SA-17. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 44.
- **G10. Root install scripts and automated security update alerts still need closure.** Keep exact versions for root dependencies, turn install scripts off where the build allows it, and turn on alerts for security updates only. Controls: CM-2, SI-2, SR-3. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g10; first milestone: Exact saves, install scripts off where possible, and security update alerts for the root package (by 2027-05-31).
- **G11. Deployment audit event coverage, forwarding and retention need evidence.** Extension, relay and hub maintainers publish the event inventory, map tested event generation and provide a supported forwarding option for required logs. The deployment operator approves the required event list and verifies representative events arrive at the configured log destination, are retained for the approved period, and can be retrieved for review. Controls: AU-2, AU-6, AU-11, SI-4. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g11; first milestone: Map the extension, relay and hub event inventory to release tests and permitted deployment log samples (Phase 44.1).
- **G13. The attestation checks do not check TCB status, certificate revocation or enclave measurements.** Check the platform's TCB status, certificate revocation and the enclave's measurements against the provider's published build; until then the security policy says so and points to the provider's full verifier. Controls: SC-8, SR-11. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g13; first milestone: TCB status, revocation and measurement checks for model attestation (by 2027-05-31).
- **G14. Staff account lifecycle needs release and deployment evidence.** Staff maintainers verify invitation approval, signed role changes and removal through the production staff and hub flow. The deployment identity owner approves eligible accounts and roles, samples an account review and offboarding, and records the approved roster and revocation results. Controls: AC-2. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g14; first milestone: Demonstrate signed staff invitation, role change and revocation against the released application with a hub (Phase 33).
- **G15. Deployment malware protection needs implementation or inheritance evidence.** The deployment sponsor and endpoint operator identify the approved malware protection provider for each in-scope workstation and hosted component. Obtain the policy and current coverage record, then record the result of an approved benign detection exercise. If a component lacks coverage, assign its deployment owner to implement the missing protection and retest. Controls: SI-3. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g15; first milestone: Reconcile the assessed component inventory with approved protection coverage, configuration and detection evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G35. Backup reliability, transfer, removal authority and cryptographic protections need evidence.** Backup operators and component maintainers inventory backups, owners and critical assets. Verify scheduled integrity and retrieval tests, separate storage and protected transfer within approved recovery targets, dual authorization for protected backup deletion, and cryptographic protection and key access. Link component restore and relay runbook evidence where applicable and assign deficiencies for implementation and retest. Controls: CP-9, CP-9(1), CP-9(3), CP-9(5), CP-9(7), CP-9(8). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g35; first milestone: Collect a timed transfer and verified restore, backup protection settings and a denied single-approver deletion result (Phase 44.1).
- **G51. Tracked as POA&M item g51; first milestone: Collect approved environment baselines and evidence of automated reconciliation, a prior baseline and a rollback exercise (Phase 44.1).

G324 records the HSM model's certificate. Sovereignty: keys. Controls: SC-12, SC-13. Owner role: shared. Planned in Phase 48.1.
- **G358. The session operator image must be rebuilt with the anchored sign-in exemption.** The operator's template gives oauth2-proxy a sign-in exemption for the monitor path that is not anchored. Starting two sessions at the same moment can fail in Theia Cloud.** Upstream Theia Cloud fails with a NullPointerException when it checks the instance limit while another new session has no status yet. Starts one at a time work, and the start page launches one session for each person. Report it upstream, and check with the load test's start bursts whether different people starting together are affected. Controls: SC-5, SI-11. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g362; first milestone: The load test's start bursts show whether starts at the same moment fail (Phase 48).

G139 covers your organization's evidence for its time settings. Controls: AU-8, SC-45. Owner role: shared. Planned in Phase 47.
- **G368. An edge clock running slow refuses valid new DID log entries.** DID log resolution must fail for an entry dated more than a few minutes ahead of the resolver's clock. Controls: AU-8, IA-5. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 71.

Sessions do not yet follow the site version.** Plan 46-09 makes each person's session run the workbench version the site has installed, so people never update by hand and every session stays compatible with its site. If a computer has verified the reduction but has yet to verify rotation of every affected cell, local writes can still use a key known to an earlier recipient whose device remains a member. Record the affected cells and pending rotations in authenticated roster state, pause local writes under the previous keys, and resume only once the new keys are verified and wrapped to cleared recipients. Keep affected writes paused until that proof or a verified rotation arrives, including across partial synchronization. Controls: AC-3, SC-12. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g552; first milestone: Prove that delayed key grants cannot allow writes under a key known to a revoked device and that unaffected cells still accept writes. (Phase 33.2).

### Does not block production {#now-does-not-block}

- **G12. The docs build is not a required check.** Make the docs check (and later the compliance check) required on main; the owner changes this repository setting, and the gap closes when the settings collector sees it. Controls: CM-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g12; first milestone: The owner makes docs a required check on main (by 2027-05-31).
- **G359. Three Theia Cloud security issues are fixed only in our build.** Upstream Theia Cloud makes the operator trust every TLS certificate for its session probe, ships the service with OIDC TLS verification set to none, and logs the service's client secret at start. Our images fix all three. File the issues with Eclipse Theia Cloud, and keep the build checks so that a version update cannot bring them back. Controls: SC-8, SC-23, IA-5. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g359; first milestone: The three issues are filed with Eclipse Theia Cloud (by 2027-03-31).
- **G361. The lab placeholder session image exits at once.** The pinned ubi9/nginx-126 placeholder prints its usage and exits, so a placeholder session never runs. The lab needs a placeholder image that keeps running for its session checks. No production site uses the placeholder. Controls: SA-11, CM-2. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 47.
- **G372. The credential test packages have no build provenance.** The Digital Bazaar packages used to test verified credentials have no build provenance, and their cryptosuite has not been updated in two years. They are used in tests only and never shipped. Keep them in test scope in the fit register, and replace them if they stop working or a maintained set appears. Controls: SR-3, SR-11. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g372; first milestone: The fit register records the packages as test scope only (Phase 71).

The extension package's size is watched, not tightly capped.** CI checks the extension package against a 64 MiB sanity ceiling and 4,000 entries, which catch an accidental inclusion such as node\_modules or source artwork; the former 14 MiB cap was self-imposed, and the owner raised it on 2026-11-25 ("keep it efficient, but it can grow"). The release-content job prints the package size and its change from main's last package, and warns when one change grows it by more than 1 MiB. Watch that report, and move large bundled data out of the package when it stops being needed. Controls: CM-2. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g373; first milestone: Large bundled data is moved out of the package when it stops being needed; the limit was reviewed on 2026-11-25 (by 2027-03-31).

Your organization decides whether people need more than one, and the design records the choice. Controls: AC-10, SC-5. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g376; first milestone: Your organization's choice on a second session is recorded (by 2027-03-31).

Complete it voluntarily before automated labelling is turned on, and share the result with your organization. Controls: RA-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g379; first milestone: The assessment is complete before automated labels apply (Phase 93).

Controls: AC-3. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g388; first milestone: The typed-in clearance is read only for replay and grants nothing (Phase 33.1).

Command A+ hosting decided: Model Vault and your organization's on-premise hosting.** Command A+ (05-2026) is Apache 2.0 (Cohere's blog, docs and Hugging Face, read 2026-11-24 and again 2026-11-25). The owner decided on 2026-11-24 that it runs through Cohere Model Vault or on your organization's own on-premise hosting under your organization's passport with its artifact hash, and not in NEAR AI's private hardware. The shipped approval follows this. Source: .planning/phases/74.1-model-passports-use-tiers-and-western-defaults/74.1-CONTEXT.md D-05. Controls: SA-4, SA-9. Owner role: owner. Planned in Phase 74.1.

Source: .planning/phases/74.1-model-passports-use-tiers-and-western-defaults/74.1-CONTEXT.md D-26. Controls: SA-4, SA-9. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g412; first milestone: NEAR AI answers how model licences pass through to your organization (N8) (by 2027-03-31).

Model exceptions are signed with a device key, not a person's credential.** An exception that lets a named senior person allow a model for chat they review exists only under your organization's rules, which list the person's key; that key is the person's device key until a credential replaces it. Your organization's operating procedure says how often edges import rules and who carries the switch to them. Source: .planning/phases/74.1-model-passports-use-tiers-and-western-defaults/74.1-CONTEXT.md D-28. Controls: AC-3, CM-6. Owner role: shared. - **G430. A late joiner starts from a checkpoint only in cells the server holds.** A person who joins a shared project late starts each log from the newest checkpoint your organization's server signed, but only in the base cell and the cells granted to that server: the server checkpoints no other cell (the trade-off of Phase 33 D-63), so there the history is read in full. Nothing is left out, and the person is told so. Phase 35, together with the server items Phase 33 D-33 moved there, decides how a late joiner starts in a cell the server cannot open. - **G431. A late joiner sees changes from an editing session open at the checkpoint only after the earlier history arrives.** Changes made after the checkpoint in an editing session that was already open at it reach a person who joins late only once the earlier history has been served, because that session registered itself before the checkpoint and its changes wait for the registration. From plan 33-32 on, the joiner's status says the earlier history is still being checked, the history is fetched in the background, and the changes then appear; before 33-32, all text from before the checkpoint waits the same way. Plan 33-33 lets such a change count at once, marked not verified, when its client's slot belongs to the change's own writer and that writer's log starts at the checkpoint, after its own threat and version-safety analysis. Source: .planning/phases/33-live-multi-user-staff-projects/33-CONTEXT.md D-70 and D-71. Controls: CP-10, SA-11. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 33.

- **G445. The development site key's private key also carries decrypt and unwrap usage.** pkcs11-tool --keypairgen --usage-sign only adds CKA\_SIGN to the private key template and never sets the other usages false (OpenSC 0.27 gen\_keypair), so SoftHSM2's defaults leave the development site key's private key with decrypt and unwrap usage as well (Usage: decrypt, sign, signRecover, unwrap; seen on a real token by deploy/test/dev-site-key-softhsm.test.mjs, 48.1-22 field fix). SoftHSM2 has no EC decrypt or unwrap mechanism and CKA\_DERIVE is false, so the extra flags cannot be used in development, and the script still requires the key to be sensitive and never extractable. Production: generate the site key in your organization's HSM with a template that sets CKA\_SIGN true and CKA\_DECRYPT, CKA\_UNWRAP and CKA\_DERIVE false (the HSM vendor's tool, or a PKCS#11 template), record the key's usage attributes in the key ceremony record (deploy/runbooks/key-ceremony.md), and add that step to the ceremony. Controls: SC-12. Owner role: shared. Planned in Phase 48.1.

## From Protected A {#protected-a}

These matter once your organization holds Protected A information.

### Blocks production {#protected-a-blocks}

The deployment information owner lists each in-scope output and its marking rule. Collect the signed test configuration, allow and refusal records, and labelled output samples. Implement and retest missing markings or document an approved scope exclusion. Controls: AC-16(2), AC-16(5). Owner role: shared. - **G17. Operational separation of duties and privileges need evidence.** Staff and gate maintainers demonstrate that role restrictions apply during approval, routine work and privileged actions, including a denial when a person holds incompatible roles. The deployment identity and security owners approve the role matrix and sample privilege reviews, separate privileged accounts, and the allowed and denied action audit records. Controls: AC-5, AC-6(1), AC-6(2), AC-6(5), AC-6(7), AC-6(9), AC-6(10). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g17; first milestone: Demonstrate the signed role and approval transitions including the dual-role self-approval refusal (Phase 33.1).

Track missing alerts or clock controls for implementation and retest. Controls: AU-5, AU-5(1), AU-8. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g18; first milestone: Collect designated alert recipients, observed failure and capacity alerts, clock configuration and a correlated event sample (Phase 44.1).

Tracked as POA&M item g33; first milestone: Record approved sites and agreements, common-risk and accessibility analysis, and a timed retrieval or failover exercise (Phase 44.1).
- **G34. Alternate telecommunications agreements and exercises need evidence.** The deployment network and service-contract owners document primary and alternate paths for in-scope processing and storage sites. Verify recovery time and service-priority provisions, provider and physical route independence, and shared points of failure. Record priority access requests when the approved scope requires them, perform scheduled failover tests, and retain the dated results and remediation. Controls: CP-8, CP-8(1), CP-8(2), CP-8(3), CP-8(5). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g34; first milestone: Collect approved telecommunications agreements and route dependencies, scope decisions and a timed failover result (Phase 44.1).
- **G36. Transaction and component recovery need scoped drills and protected inputs.** Deployment recovery operators and component maintainers identify transaction-based stores, critical components and protected recovery tools. Exercise rollback or journal recovery on each applicable transaction store and restore components from approved integrity-checked baselines. Measure time to known operational state, verify protection and access limits on recovery components, and record sponsor decisions for inapplicable objectives. Controls: CP-10, CP-10(2), CP-10(4), CP-10(6). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g36; first milestone: Capture applicable transaction repair, timed reconstitution from known baselines, and reviewed recovery tool access (Phase 44.1).
- **G37. Failed sign-in limits and responses need deployment evidence.** The deployment identity owner approves the failed-attempt threshold, time window and automatic response for each applicable sign-in path. The sign-in operator records the active settings. Using authorized test accounts, verify the response when the limit is exceeded and collect redacted results for the required lock, delay, notification or recovery behavior. Record inherited mechanisms and assign gaps to the responsible component or provider. Controls: AC-7. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g37; first milestone: Collect the approved failed-attempt policy and configuration and an observed threshold and recovery exercise for each sign-in path (Phase 44.1).
- **G38. System use notices and actions before authentication need review.** The sponsor approves the notice text with privacy and security owners and documents each action allowed before authentication with its rationale in the system security plan. Interface and service operators inventory public and restricted entry points. Collect redacted captures of notice timing and required acknowledgment before access, and test that approved public actions work while protected actions require authentication. Record any distinct notice for publicly accessible systems. Controls: AC-8, AC-14. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g38; first milestone: Approve the notices and anonymous action inventory and collect entry-point screenshots, acknowledgment and access decision evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G39. Device locking and obscured displays need endpoint evidence.** The deployment endpoint owner records which workstations and managed devices are in scope. The sponsor approves inactivity thresholds and unattended locking rules. Collect managed settings and redacted captures showing the inactivity or manual lock as applicable, previously visible information concealed by a publicly viewable lock display, and access restored only through approved authentication. Assign missing inherited or component controls for implementation and retest. Controls: AC-11, AC-11(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g39; first milestone: Verify endpoint coverage, configured lock rules, obscured displays and authenticated unlock using the deployed platform settings (Phase 44.1).
- **G40. Inactivity logout and logical session termination need evidence.** Deployment identity and session operators identify in-scope local, browser and remote user sessions. The sponsor approves when users must log out and the conditions for automatic session termination. Collect the approved user procedure and deployed settings. Exercise the configured triggers and verify that the old session cannot continue or regain protected access. Record any approved work allowed to continue after termination and its access boundary. Controls: AC-2(5), AC-12. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g40; first milestone: Collect the inactivity logout procedure, effective session configuration and redacted termination and expired-session denial results (Phase 44.1).
- **G41. Remote access methods and privileged access need deployment evidence.** The sponsor authorizes each applicable remote access method and documents its conditions and privileged-use rationale in the system security plan. Network and service operators record managed entry points, monitoring and control settings, session cryptographic configuration and approved dedicated management consoles. Collect redacted tests for allowed access, denied unapproved paths and denied privileged access from ordinary endpoints, plus trustworthy records of authorized remote privileged commands and access to security-relevant information. Controls: AC-17, AC-17(1), AC-17(2), AC-17(3), AC-17(4), AC-17(400). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g41; first milestone: Approve the remote-access inventory and collect managed path, session protection, monitoring and privileged-operation evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G42. External system use and storage restrictions need deployment evidence.** The sponsor identifies which external systems may access the deployment or process, store or transmit its information. Deployment operators verify those systems against approved security and privacy controls and retain applicable connection or processing agreements. Record authorized restrictions for portable storage and prohibited network-accessible storage. Collect the approved system inventory, verification records and representative permitted and refused access and storage tests, with evidence references for sensitive agreements. Controls: AC-20, AC-20(1), AC-20(2), AC-20(4). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g42; first milestone: Review external-system applicability and collect control verification, agreements, removable and network storage settings and representative test receipts (Phase 44.1).
- **G43. Information-sharing safeguards and agreements need deployment evidence.** The sponsor and information owner identify applicable sharing with external public-sector organizations and sharing between or within federal institutions. Retain authorized references to the applicable written agreements or arrangements and their safeguarding terms. Component and deployment operators demonstrate how users compare partner authorization to the information restrictions and collect redacted results for allowed and disallowed sharing. Reuse approved export-control evidence only for that part of the assessed boundary. Controls: AC-21, AC-21(400), AC-21(401). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g43; first milestone: Approve sharing scope and verify signed agreements or arrangements, partner authorization rules and allowed and denied information transfers (Phase 44.1).
- **G44. Deployment audit and accountability policy needs approval and operating records.** The deployment audit policy owner approves the scope, roles, responsibilities and audit procedures with the component and monitoring owners. Record who received the policy, its accountable official and review triggers, and confirm the procedures reflect the deployment boundary and applicable obligations. Controls: AU-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g44; first milestone: Collect the approved policy and procedures, distribution record and evidence of their required review (Phase 44.1).
- **G45. Selected component events and audit record fields need coverage evidence.** Extension, relay and hub maintainers map the approved AU-02 event inventory to generation tests for every assessed component. Capture redacted records proving event type, time, component or location, source, outcome and relevant actor or entity, plus each approved additional field. The deployment audit owner approves the list and verifies who can select the events. Document adjustments and retest omissions without exposing secrets or record payloads. Controls: AU-3, AU-3(1), AU-12. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g45; first milestone: Collect the approved event and field matrix, authorized event-selection evidence and redacted records from each assessed source (Phase 44.1).
- **G46. Audit capacity planning and offloading need measured deployment evidence.** The deployment logging operator and component owners document expected and peak volumes, retention, local buffer limits and capacity for all assessed sources. Verify scheduled offloading of audit records to the designated separate store and reconcile a measured sample from production and retrieval. Exercise delivery loss and recovery, track any unforwarded records, and retest gaps. Use Phase 84 for the relay runbook when the relay is in scope. Controls: AU-4, AU-4(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g46; first milestone: Collect approved capacity and offload configuration with a volume sample, delivery reconciliation and recorded recovery (Phase 44.1).
- **G47. Audit review, centralized analysis and time correlation need operating evidence.** Deployment monitoring and incident response owners approve review cadence, review triggers, reporting recipients, and the sources and clock tolerance for a system-wide trail. Component maintainers provide redacted event samples. Demonstrate central review, correlation across repositories and automated routing of a harmless test event to the approved response process. Record measured clock tolerance, owner review and follow-up, then assign and retest coverage gaps. Controls: AU-6, AU-6(1), AU-6(3), AU-6(4), AU-12(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g47; first milestone: Collect approved review and source settings, a time-correlated multi-source record and a documented alert handoff and review (Phase 44.1).
- **G48. Audit analysis and reports need authorized field searches and source integrity evidence.** The deployment audit analyst and reporting system owner identify approved search and sorting fields and the reporting tool. Generate an on-demand review and a representative incident report from sanitized source records. Compare source checksums and record order before and after reduction to verify that the tool preserves original records. Assign missing capabilities to the component or monitoring owner and retest. Controls: AU-7, AU-7(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g48; first milestone: Collect approved query fields, representative query and report results, and before-and-after source integrity and ordering receipts (Phase 44.1).
- **G49. Audit infrastructure separation, privileged roles and protection alerts need evidence.** Deployment logging and identity owners review the audit store topology and approved separation frequency. Verify the store is on a physically different system or component where required. Review the privileged roles authorized to administer logging, and the separate read-only roles. Test allowed reads, denied changes and deletions, and delivery of unauthorized-change alerts through an approved exercise. Component maintainers preserve scoped file permission evidence and investigate missing protection. Controls: AU-9, AU-9(2), AU-9(4), AU-9(6). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g49; first milestone: Collect approved topology and privileged role assignments, redacted access checks, and a verified unauthorized-change alert receipt (Phase 44.1).
- **G50. Configuration policy and management plan need deployment approval.** The deployment configuration manager obtains sponsor approval for the policy and management plan. Record accountable roles, approved items under configuration control, management and change procedures, protections for the plan, and distribution and review records. Collect a sampled application of the approved workflow. Controls: CM-1, CM-9. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g50; first milestone: Collect the approved policy and plan, accountable roles, distribution and a sampled change trace (Phase 44.1).
- **G52. High-risk travel device configuration and return evidence need approved scope.** The sponsor and endpoint security owner identify approved high-risk travel conditions and devices. Verify provisioning from the restricted baseline, authorized assignment and required measures on return. Retain an approved baseline and redacted provisioning and return sample, or the authorized scope decision. Controls: CM-2(7). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g52; first milestone: Collect the approved travel rules, device baseline and issued-and-returned device evidence or approved scope disposition (Phase 44.1).
- **G53. Deployment change decisions, impacts and authorized access need a verified change trace.** Release maintainers and deployment change authority sample a configuration-controlled change. Record security and privacy impact review with named representatives, approval or refusal, effective access restrictions, isolated test validation, monitored change deployment and post-change verification of each affected control. Include review records and applicable authorized-access decisions. Use G7 and G12 only for their scoped repository evidence. Controls: CM-3, CM-3(2), CM-3(4), CM-4, CM-4(1), CM-4(2), CM-5. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g53; first milestone: Collect one approved change with pre-change analysis, restricted access, separate test evidence and operating-control checks after deployment (Phase 44.1).
- **G54. Secure settings, least-functionality review and approved execution need evidence.** Component maintainers and deployment security operators approve the applicable restrictive baseline and essential functions, ports, protocols, services and software. Compare applied settings to the approved baseline, record authorized exceptions and monitoring, review unused functions, and test permitted and denied program execution under the approved allow-by-exception policy. Record gaps in deployed host or application enforcement and retest. Controls: CM-6, CM-7, CM-7(1), CM-7(2), CM-7(5). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g54; first milestone: Collect signed settings and exceptions, reviewed service inventory, change monitoring, and allowed and denied execution receipts (Phase 44.1).
- **G55. Installed components need accountable inventory and automated unauthorized component response.** Deployment asset and component owners reconcile scoped assets, responsible administrators, assessed configurations and approved deviations with installation, removal and update records. Demonstrate approved automated detection using a synthetic unauthorized component and record the configured response. Use release inventories as evidence for supplier artifacts and verify actual deployments independently. Controls: CM-8, CM-8(1), CM-8(3), CM-8(4), CM-8(6). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g55; first milestone: Collect signed inventory reconciliation, administrator and deviation records, and a sanitized unauthorized-component detection and response receipt (Phase 44.1).
- **G56. Software use, licences and privileged user installations need operating evidence.** Deployment software asset and endpoint administration owners approve installation and peer-to-peer use rules. Record applicable licence entitlements and reconcile constrained quantities. Demonstrate allowed privileged installation, denied ordinary-user installation and monitoring. Collect software exception and peer-to-peer restrictions where applicable and track implementation gaps. Controls: CM-10, CM-11, CM-11(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g56; first milestone: Collect entitlement and installation policy records, an approved and refused installation, monitoring receipts and any applicable sharing restrictions (Phase 44.1).
- **G57. Information locations, access and automated discovery need scoped deployment evidence.** The deployment data steward and component maintainers inventory approved information types, processing and storage locations, and users with access. Include approved provider, relay, hub and local scope as applicable. Sample authorized location changes and test the approved automated discovery tool against seeded benign data in each assessed component. Record scope or sensing gaps for follow-up and preserve only sanitized references. Controls: CM-12, CM-12(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g57; first milestone: Collect the approved information location and access inventory, reviewed location change and scoped automated discovery results (Phase 44.1).
- **G58. Deployment access control policy needs approval and evidence.** The deployment sponsor designates the access control policy owner and approves the policy and operating procedures for the assessed system. The policy owner records scope, responsibilities, coordination and distribution, and sets review intervals and triggers. Retain the signed version, named owner, dissemination record and schedule and samples for policy and procedure review. Controls: AC-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g58; first milestone: Collect the approved deployment access control policy, procedures, named owner and dissemination and review records (Phase 44.1).
- **G59. Account automation, disablement and audit need deployment evidence.** The deployment identity owner approves managed account types, automated lifecycle mechanisms, expiry and inactivity limits, high-risk criteria and disablement deadlines. Using authorized test identities, verify temporary and emergency expiry, disablement for expiration, inactivity, separation, policy violation and significant risk, and automatic auditing of creation, modification, enabling, disabling and removal. Retain redacted event and timing evidence. The catalogue incorporates shared-account credential changes into AC-02. Reconcile the selected AC-02(10) row with the sponsor, recording AC-02 evidence for any shared accounts and an approved tailoring decision. Controls: AC-2(1), AC-2(2), AC-2(3), AC-2(4), AC-2(10), AC-2(13). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g59; first milestone: Collect approved lifecycle rules, automation and timed disablement results, audit records and the documented AC-02(10) reconciliation (Phase 44.1).
- **G60. Privileged account assignment and removal need monitoring evidence.** The deployment identity owner approves the role-based or attribute-based scheme and the authorities who assign privileged accounts. Account operators inventory applicable privileged assignments and monitor changes. Collect redacted configuration, sampled approved assignments, change-monitoring records and timely revocation evidence. Verify that a removed assignment cannot use the privileged action. Controls: AC-2(7). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g60; first milestone: Collect approved privileged account inventory, role or attribute change monitoring, and denial after revocation (Phase 44.1).
- **G61. Dual authorization for designated actions needs evidence.** The deployment sponsor and privilege owners identify actions with significant impact that require separate authorized approvers. Implement or verify enforcement for those actions and retain the approved action and approver mapping. Exercise denial with one approver, denial when the same identity attempts both approvals, and success with two eligible approvers. Where relevant, use the product gate's per-action decision evidence as input and verify the second independent approval at the assessed enforcement boundary. Controls: AC-3(2). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g61; first milestone: Approve actions requiring dual authorization and retain denied single or duplicate approvals and accepted independent approvals (Phase 44.1).
- **G62. Discretionary access decisions need scoped permission evidence.** The sponsor and access policy owner identify the subjects, objects and discretionary access policy in scope. Component and deployment operators verify how authorized holders may share information, delegate privileges, set or change attributes, or change access rules, where the policy permits those actions. Collect the reviewed policy and exact-release allowed and refused results. Include the staff roster and cell access rules only for the component and operations those rules govern. Controls: AC-3(4). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g62; first milestone: Approve the discretionary access boundary and verify release and deployment allow and denial evidence for each applicable operation (Phase 44.1).
- **G63. Controlled information release needs destination and approval evidence.** The sponsor and information release owner define what may leave the system, which receiving systems are eligible and which safeguards and validation they require. Operators and component maintainers verify configured release routes and content validation for each applicable channel. Retain approved policies, receiver safeguard evidence and redacted records of releases allowed and refused for content or destination. Use model-route and export eligibility evidence only for the routes it covers. Controls: AC-3(9). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g63; first milestone: Approve release boundaries and collect recipient safeguard and release validation evidence for each in-scope channel (Phase 44.1).
- **G64. Wireless access and configuration restrictions need deployment evidence.** The sponsor authorizes each permitted wireless access type and appoints the wireless network and endpoint administrators. Collect the approved inventory and configuration requirements, effective encryption and required user or device authentication settings, pre-issuance evidence for disabled unused radios and the authorized wireless configurator roles. Exercise admission and refusal for the approved boundary and verify that unauthorized roles cannot change wireless settings. Controls: AC-18, AC-18(1), AC-18(3), AC-18(4). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g64; first milestone: Collect authorized wireless scope, deployed settings, disabled-radio and configuration-role evidence and permitted and refused connection tests (Phase 44.1).
- **G65. Managed mobile access and encryption need deployment evidence.** The sponsor and endpoint management owner identify and authorize organization-controlled mobile devices, including use outside controlled areas, and approve the required full-device or container encryption. Collect the approved fleet and enrollment scope, effective device management and encryption settings, and redacted tests showing that conforming devices can connect and unapproved or nonconforming devices are refused. Record inheritances and reviewed exclusions. Where collectors are deployed, use their enrollment records only for their device binding. Controls: AC-19, AC-19(5). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g65; first milestone: Collect approved mobile connection scope, managed device and encryption reports, and allowed and denied access results (Phase 44.1).
- **G66. Public posting authority and content review need operating evidence.** The sponsor designates authorized public publishers and names the privacy or security reviewer and the operator who can remove content. Document the assessed public channels and capture publisher authorization and training, a prepublication review record, the recurring review schedule and completed sample, and an approved removal exercise or a real redacted removal record. Identify the review and release process for each public channel in scope. Controls: AC-22. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g66; first milestone: Collect approved public channel and publisher lists, training, initial and recurring content reviews and a removal record (Phase 44.1).
- **G67. System integrity policy and procedures need approved operating evidence.** The sponsor system integrity lead approves the policy and procedures, identifies component and operations responsibilities, and records coordination, distribution and review. Verify a representative flaw, protection or monitoring work item followed the approved procedure. Controls: SI-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g67; first milestone: Collect the approved policy, named roles, review and distribution records and a sampled operating action (Phase 44.1).
- **G69. Malware protection updates need privileged authorization and activity evidence.** Deployment endpoint and hosted security owners identify each malware protection update mechanism and its privileged approving role. Verify a permitted update and denial for an ordinary role or unauthorized configuration change. Capture redacted policy and audit receipts from each assessed protection mechanism and track uncovered assets through G15. Controls: SI-3(4). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g69; first milestone: Collect approved update authority and observed privileged update and denied unprivileged change evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G71. Deployed integrity checks and violation response need tested coverage.** Component maintainers and deployment integrity and incident response owners approve the software, firmware and information to verify, checking schedule and recipients. Demonstrate centrally managed settings and notifications by detecting a harmless changed test artifact, then record incident intake and corrective action. Use G4 attestations as supplier provenance and verify deployed monitoring and response separately. Controls: SI-7, SI-7(1), SI-7(2), SI-7(3), SI-7(7). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g71; first milestone: Collect approved integrity coverage, check schedule and central configuration, a detected change receipt, and the incident handling record (Phase 44.1).
- **G72. Message boundary spam protection and automatic updates need verified applicability.** The deployment messaging and endpoint owners identify applicable message ingress and egress and the protection mechanism supplied by each assessed provider. Verify approved automatic update cadence and detection and action for harmless simulated unsolicited messages on each applicable boundary. Obtain authorized scope treatment for unused messaging surfaces. Controls: SI-8, SI-8(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g72; first milestone: Collect applicable mail or messaging protection settings, update history and a sanitized detection and response sample (Phase 44.1).
- **G73. Component input validation and role-scoped errors need traceable tests.** Component maintainers and deployment security owners inventory approved input surfaces and error audiences for the extension, relay and hub as assessed. Run benign invalid input, malformed message and out-of-scope data tests and verify safe refusal and permitted diagnostic detail. Capture redacted user and operator error samples and verify sensitive values remain absent. Assign and retest uncovered interfaces. Controls: SI-10, SI-11. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g73; first milestone: Collect a scoped interface and error-audience matrix and exact test receipts for invalid input, safe responses and redacted diagnostics (Phase 44.1).
- **G74. Managed memory protections and dedicated administration workstations need deployment evidence.** The deployment endpoint and privileged access owners identify assessed processes and the approved host memory-execution protections. Verify those settings on sampled assessed hosts. Separately inventory dedicated physical administration workstations and allowed task and network boundaries, show their isolation and verify privileged actions are restricted to the approved workstations. Record approved scope decisions and gaps. Controls: SI-16, SI-400. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g74; first milestone: Collect host hardening settings and separate evidence of administration workstation inventory, isolation, and authorized and refused privileged access (Phase 44.1).
- **G75. Assessment policy and risk treatment decisions need authority and follow-up evidence.** The sponsor risk authority approves risk assessment and response procedures, owners, review triggers and tolerance. Sample an actual finding through assignment, accepted treatment or remediation, authorized approval and follow-up. Record scope, residual risk, review or expiry date and reassessment responsibility. Controls: RA-1, RA-7. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g75; first milestone: Collect the approved policy and a sampled finding with assigned response, disposition authority and follow-up evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G76. System sensitivity, risks and critical dependencies need assessed deployment evidence.** The sponsor categorization and risk owners approve information impact and handling decisions. Component maintainers supply current data flows and trust boundaries. Review the actual deployment threat and privacy risks, critical assets and supporting dependencies and verify traceability to selected safeguards and open actions. Controls: RA-2, RA-3, RA-9. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g76; first milestone: Collect the approved categorization and rationale, assessed deployment risk record and approved criticality analysis (Phase 44.1).
- **G77. Supply chain risk assessments need reviewed service and dependency scope.** The deployment procurement and risk owners identify assessed suppliers, services, release dependencies and trust boundaries. Release maintainers supply available inventory and provenance. Assess concentration, integrity and continuity risks, record owners and treatments, and retain the review trigger and date. Use supplier evidence and approved exception references rather than unverified assertions. Controls: RA-3(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g77; first milestone: Collect scoped supplier and dependency inventory, approved supply chain risk findings and dated treatment or review records (Phase 44.1).
- **G78. Vulnerability monitoring needs current coverage and bounded scan authority.** The deployment vulnerability management owner approves scope, schedule, coverage, detection content updates and any authorized elevated scanner identities. Reconcile scoped assets against inventory and verify current detection content and authorized access in a permitted test environment. Review and track redacted results. Preserve exact release inventory checks and verify deployments separately. Controls: RA-5, RA-5(2), RA-5(5). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g78; first milestone: Collect the scoped monitoring schedule, recorded detection content version and authorized scan-role evidence with a redacted result and follow-up (Phase 44.1).
- **G79. Public reporting instructions and private vulnerability intake need an exercised handoff.** Product security and deployment intake owners verify the published instructions reach the approved private channel. Exercise a clearly marked benign report through receipt, triage and owner handoff, retaining restricted and redacted evidence. Record how deployed services receive reports or inherit the approved organizational route. Controls: RA-5(11). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g79; first milestone: Collect published reporting instructions, destination verification and a redacted test receipt and handoff by the authorized owner (Phase 44.1).
- **G80. System security and privacy plans need approved deployment scope and diagrams.** The sponsor security and privacy owners approve planning policy and procedures, named responsibilities and the assessed boundary. Complete the system security and privacy plan with current component and trust-boundary diagrams, data flows, roles, requirements, shared responsibilities, exceptions and links to assessor evidence. Record review and release or deployment change triggers. Controls: PL-1, PL-2, PL-8. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g80; first milestone: Collect the approved planning procedures, system security and privacy plan, reviewed deployment diagrams and linked evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G81. Rules of behaviour and external-site restrictions need acknowledged deployment records.** Deployment access and privacy owners approve rules of behaviour and external application and public posting restrictions. Verify the rules reach assigned users, acknowledgements or equivalent authorized records exist before access and on revision, and applicable external access restrictions have an operating sample. Record approved scope for external services. Controls: PL-4, PL-4(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g81; first milestone: Collect approved rules and restrictions, a redacted acknowledgement and dated sample of the applicable enforcement or approval process (Phase 44.1).
- **G82. Selected control baselines and tailoring need authorized decisions.** The sponsor security and privacy authorities approve the applicable baseline and overlays using categorization and deployment boundaries. Link every inclusion, enhancement, inheritance, exclusion or alternative to its rationale, affected control and component, approving authority and evidence or open action. Reassess the baseline when the release, configuration or scope changes. Controls: PL-10, PL-11. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g82; first milestone: Collect the approved baseline and tailoring register with reviewed control-level rationale, authority and outstanding evidence paths (Phase 44.1).
- **G83. Response training and coordinated exercises need dated deployment evidence.** The deployment incident response lead assigns role-specific training and exercise cadence, then coordinates a representative drill with continuity, privacy and other applicable plan owners. Retain attendance, scope, scenario, measured performance, corrective actions and follow-up retest. Use supplier drills only for the exercised component and event. Controls: IR-2, IR-3, IR-3(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g83; first milestone: Collect training history, approved scenario and coordination records, exercise results and retested corrective actions (Phase 44.1).
- **G84. Incident handling and continuity actions need a tested response trace.** The deployment response and continuity leads and component maintainers identify incident classes, required mission continuity actions and approved dynamic response mechanisms. Exercise a benign declared event through detection, analysis, containment, recovery and a continuity decision. Record the authorized roles, measured transitions, tool readiness and follow-up. Controls: IR-4, IR-4(3), IR-4(9). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g84; first milestone: Collect an approved response and continuity scenario with dated decisions, recovery checks and observed dynamic response (Phase 44.1).
- **G85. External incident correlation and information sharing need authorized evidence.** The sponsor response lead, privacy authority and approved external partners agree the incident information categories, purpose, recipient, handling and coordination procedure. Demonstrate an authorized sanitized exchange and correlation in a drill. Keep an approved agreement or equivalent record, its scope and evidence reference. Controls: IR-4(8). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g85; first milestone: Collect the approved partner scope and sharing terms, plus a sanitized exchange and correlation exercise record (Phase 44.1).
- **G86. Incident tracking and automated reporting need demonstrated handoffs.** The deployment incident operations, vulnerability and supplier coordination owners define tracking fields, reporting times, approved recipients and mechanisms. Exercise a synthetic incident through tracking, authorized automated notification, related flaw disclosure and applicable supplier handoff. Retain delivery and acknowledgement timestamps, recorded disposition and evidence of restricted recipients. Controls: IR-5, IR-6, IR-6(1), IR-6(2), IR-6(3). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g86; first milestone: Collect a sanitized tracking record and timed automated, vulnerability and applicable supplier notification and acknowledgement receipts (Phase 44.1).
- **G87. Incident reporting assistance and automated availability need an exercised user path.** The deployment incident support owner publishes the approved assistance route to users and reviews automated information delivery and access. Exercise a benign request from an allowed user, verify timely assistance and assigned escalation, and retain sanitized evidence that support guidance and intake were reachable under normal and degraded conditions. Controls: IR-7, IR-7(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g87; first milestone: Collect approved support instructions, scoped availability settings and a dated help request, response and escalation exercise (Phase 44.1).
- **G89. Supply chain risk policy, plan and team need approved operating evidence.** The sponsor supply chain risk official approves the policy, procedures and protected lifecycle plan for assessed components and services. Name the team and coordinator across acquisition, operations, security and disposal. Record who receives and reviews the documents, their access controls and review triggers, and a dated coordination decision. Controls: SR-1, SR-2, SR-2(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g89; first milestone: Collect approved policy and plan references, assigned team roles, distribution and access records, and a sampled review decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G90. Acquisition safeguards need evidence from a reviewed procurement.** The contracting authority and deployment procurement lead identify acquisition safeguards for assessed goods and services. Sample an acquisition using documented selection criteria, integrity and provenance requirements, supplier obligations and acceptance decisions. Record any exceptions and their approval. Controls: SR-5. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g90; first milestone: Collect a redacted acquisition record linking approved risk criteria, contract safeguards and a dated acceptance or refusal (Phase 44.1).
- **G91. Supplier assessments and treatment of supply chain findings need evidence.** The deployment supplier assurance lead and component maintainers identify in-scope suppliers, delivered components and services, reviewers and assessment cadence. Review a representative supplier against approved requirements. Record the finding, selected safeguards in the supply chain or system plans, corrective action owner, follow-up and disposition. Use G10 for scoped root dependency safeguards and G77 for the supply chain risk assessment. Controls: SR-3, SR-6. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g91; first milestone: Collect a dated supplier review, selected control references, and a sampled weakness through treatment and follow-up (Phase 44.1).
- **G92. Supplier notification agreements and escalation routes need verification.** The deployment contracting and incident response leads review notification agreements for assessed suppliers. Verify what triggers notice, the reporting time, approved contacts and permitted information sharing. Product security supplies applicable advisory procedures. Exercise a harmless supplier notification and retain a redacted receipt, acknowledgement and escalation record. Controls: SR-8. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g92; first milestone: Collect signed agreement references, contact and timing rules, and a redacted notification exercise receipt (Phase 44.1).
- **G93. Tamper inspection needs approved triggers and observed acceptance evidence.** The deployment acceptance manager and component custodians identify the items and events that require inspection. For assessed software, verify expected artifact digests and provenance before acceptance and exercise refusal of a harmless changed copy. For assessed physical items, record approved seal and custody checks and their disposition. Use existing release attestations as a supplier input. Controls: SR-10. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g93; first milestone: Collect an approved inspection procedure, a verified sample, and a recorded refusal or quarantine from a harmless tamper exercise (Phase 44.1).
- **G94. Component authenticity procedures and anti-counterfeit training need evidence.** The sponsor component assurance lead and supplier maintainers establish trusted acquisition and authenticity checks for the assessed component types. Name reporting recipients and roles that detect suspect hardware, software or firmware. Verify required training and a harmless detection and escalation exercise. Use G4 and G13 for their scoped provenance and attestation receipts. Controls: SR-11, SR-11(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g94; first milestone: Collect approved authenticity and reporting procedures, role-based training records, and a redacted detection and escalation exercise (Phase 44.1).
- **G95. Service and repair components need controlled configuration and return records.** The maintenance authority and component custodian identify assessed components subject to service or repair. Sample approved custody and baseline records before service, authorized changes and access while held, and verification against the approved configuration before return to service. Record any variance and the decision to release or retain the component. Controls: SR-11(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g95; first milestone: Collect a redacted service record with custody, authorized changes, post-service verification and return approval (Phase 44.1).
- **G96. Component disposal needs approved methods and custody evidence.** The asset custodian and disposal authority identify assessed components and approved disposal or sanitization methods by component and information sensitivity. Track a representative item through approved removal and custody transfer, method verification, and dated disposition. Retain an authorized disposal receipt and reconcile the inventory. Controls: SR-12. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g96; first milestone: Collect approved disposal methods, a redacted custody and disposal receipt, and the reconciled inventory update (Phase 44.1).
- **G97. Assessment policy and independent assessment need approved records.** The sponsor assessment lead obtains approved policy, procedures and a scoped assessment plan with controls, methods, environments, responsibilities and reporting dates. Record the assessor appointment and independence determination. Collect the dated assessment results, evidence references, sponsor distribution and retained findings. Controls: CA-1, CA-2, CA-2(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g97; first milestone: Collect the approved policy and plan, assessor appointment and independence decision, and reviewed assessment results (Phase 44.1).
- **G98. External exchange and internal connection authorization need reviewed evidence.** The sponsor boundary owner and privacy authority inventory internal connections and external exchanges separately. Approve interfaces, information types, safeguards, owners and review rules. Retain an approved external agreement and a sampled internal configuration and security and privacy check before connection, as applicable. Record approved review, termination conditions and any exceptions. Controls: CA-3, CA-9, CA-9(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g98; first milestone: Collect approved exchange and connection register entries, applicable agreements and an assessed preconnection safeguard check (Phase 44.1).
- **G99. Deployment POA&M needs tracked ownership and revision evidence.** The sponsor remediation authority records assessment findings and known weaknesses with owners, milestones and closure receipts. Approve the review cadence and sampled updates when results change. Link the deployment register to the product POA&M where relevant and retain independent assessor dispositions for closures. Controls: CA-5. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g99; first milestone: Collect the approved deployment POA&M and a sampled change from initial finding through dated action or reviewed closure (Phase 44.1).
- **G100. Authorization and inherited control decisions need designated officials and signed records.** The sponsor designates system and common-control authorizing officials, reviews the submitted scope, assessment and outstanding risks, and records authorization conditions, duration and review triggers. Keep the formal signed decision or current authorized submission step, including approved inherited-control responsibilities. Update scope decisions when significant changes occur. Controls: CA-6. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g100; first milestone: Collect formal appointments, the actual assessment submission, scoped inheritance decisions and the signed authorization or authorized outstanding decision step (Phase 44.1).
- **G101. Continuous monitoring needs independent reviews and operating risk evidence.** The deployment monitoring and risk leads approve metrics, collection and review frequencies, reporting authority and the independent assessment arrangement. Component maintainers provide scoped evidence sources. Sample effectiveness, obligation and change monitoring results, findings and response decisions. Record escalation and follow-up within the approved deployment scope. Controls: CA-7, CA-7(1), CA-7(4). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g101; first milestone: Collect the approved monitoring strategy, independent assessor assignment, metrics samples and an evidenced risk review and response (Phase 44.1).
- **G102. System and services acquisition policy and procedures need approved operating records.** The sponsor acquisition policy official approves scope, procedures, accountable procurement, security and privacy roles, distribution and review triggers. Sample one applicable procurement through the documented process and retain evidence of review and any exception. Controls: SA-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g102; first milestone: Collect approved policy and procedures, role assignment, distribution and review records, and a sampled acquisition decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G103. Security and privacy resource commitments need approved budget evidence.** The sponsor business owner and financial authority map high-level security and privacy requirements to planned people, services and funds. Retain the dated investment decision and discrete security and privacy budget allocation. Record the authority and follow-up for any shortfall or change. Controls: SA-2. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g103; first milestone: Collect approved requirements, an investment decision, a redacted budget line and the disposition of a sampled allocation change (Phase 44.1).
- **G104. Lifecycle security and privacy roles and risk reviews need operating evidence.** The sponsor system owner and development lead identify the lifecycle stages, accountable people and review gates for each assessed component or service. Trace a selected requirement and risk from acquisition or design through testing and release, with owners, dated approvals and a follow-up disposition. Controls: SA-3. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g104; first milestone: Collect the approved lifecycle and named role assignments, a security and privacy requirement trace, and a dated lifecycle risk decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G105. Acquisition contracts need traceable security, privacy and interface acceptance evidence.** The contracting authority, sponsor technical lead and supplier identify assessed acquisitions and approved contract language. Trace functional, strength and assurance requirements, documentation protection, development and operating environments, assigned responsibilities and acceptance criteria to contract clauses. Keep the supplier description of control behavior and required functions, ports, protocols and services, and a reviewed acceptance sample. Controls: SA-4, SA-4(1), SA-4(9). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g105; first milestone: Collect signed or otherwise approved contract references, a supplier control and interface specification, and a sampled acceptance disposition (Phase 44.1).
- **G106. Digital credential products need validated recommendation and procurement evidence.** The sponsor identity assurance and procurement leads identify the credential products used by assessed systems and the required assurance and robustness levels. Match the exact product and configuration to Cyber Centre recommendation evidence obtained through the designated authority at acquisition or review. Record selection and acceptance or remediation for any unmatched product. Controls: SA-4(10). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g106; first milestone: Collect the approved identity requirements, exact product and configuration inventory, current recommendation evidence and a signed acquisition disposition (Phase 44.1).
- **G107. Contractor data ownership, return and removal need verified records.** The contracting authority and sponsor data owner identify applicable suppliers and contract terms for ownership, the return deadline and removal from contractor systems. Verify a completed exit or approved exercise, reconcile the returned inventory with the original scope, and review the supplier removal evidence, backups, authorized retention and exceptions. Controls: SA-4(12). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g107; first milestone: Collect signed ownership and exit clauses, a dated return receipt and reconciliation, and verified removal or authorized retention records (Phase 44.1).
- **G108. Administrator and user documentation and training need versioned delivery evidence.** The deployment service owner and supplier leads identify documentation and training for assessed controls and user roles. Verify secure installation and operation guidance, known configuration weaknesses, user privacy responsibilities and an administrator and user training sample. Record attempts to obtain missing guidance, approved next actions, distribution and training completion. Preserve X12 as the specific export-control guidance path. Controls: SA-5, SA-16. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g108; first milestone: Collect versioned user and administrator guidance, distribution receipts, missing-document dispositions, and dated training and operating exercise evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G109. Engineering principles and developer security and privacy design need reviewed traces.** The sponsor security and privacy architects approve applicable engineering principles and scope. Supplier architects link those principles and required controls to design decisions, component allocations and interdependent security and privacy functions. Review the design with the organization architecture owner and trace an implemented decision to its exact verification evidence. Use G9 for scoped threat models and data flows. Controls: SA-8, SA-17. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g109; first milestone: Collect approved principles, reviewed architecture and component-control allocations, and a sampled design-to-verification trace (Phase 44.1).
- **G111. In-scope processing and storage locations need verified Canadian boundary evidence.** The sponsor data residency authority and service operator map every assessed processing and storage location, including replicas, backups, failover and relevant subprocessors. Obtain provider and deployment configuration evidence for where processing and storage occur, then demonstrate an assessed location restriction. Record and escalate unverified or out-of-bound flows for remediation. Sovereignty: data-stored, ai-runs, assessments. Controls: SA-9(8). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g111; first milestone: Collect reviewed data flows, provider and region evidence, deployment location settings, and a dated restriction verification (Phase 44.1).
- **G112. Developer change control and security and privacy review need exact change evidence.** The sponsor change authority and developer configuration lead agree control scope across approved lifecycle stages and designate security and privacy reviewers and flaw-report recipients. Trace a representative change using the protected baseline, approval, impact assessment, changed configuration, and evidence that unauthorized changes are refused. Record a tracked flaw through resolution and reporting. Controls: SA-10, SA-10(7). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g112; first milestone: Collect change-control scope and named reviewers, an approved change and impact trace, and the linked flaw and reporting records (Phase 44.1).
- **G113. Delivered software and firmware integrity verification needs a tested acceptance record.** The developer release lead and deployment acceptance authority identify assessed software and firmware, including applicable updates. Verify exact artifact signatures, digests or provenance against independently trusted release information. Exercise refusal of a harmless mismatched artifact and retain the result for each applicable artifact class. Use existing artifact attestations for the release components they cover. Controls: SA-10(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g113; first milestone: Collect approved verification scope, an accepted artifact and provenance reference, and a recorded mismatch refusal (Phase 44.1).
- **G114. Developer control testing and verifiable flaw correction need reviewed release evidence.** The sponsor assessment lead and developer assurance lead approve the post-design assessment plan, test methods, scope and frequency for security and privacy controls. Retain evidence of test execution and the reviewed result. Trace a flaw through triage, correction and exact-version retest with acceptance or disposition of unresolved findings. Use G6 for scoped static analysis. Controls: SA-11. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g114; first milestone: Collect the approved assessment plan, a versioned execution report, and a finding traced through fix and retest (Phase 44.1).
- **G115. Developer process, tools and criticality decisions need controlled records.** The sponsor development assurance lead and supplier engineering lead approve security and privacy development requirements, tool and standard versions, options, integrity controls and change review. At designated lifecycle decision points, assess the criticality of scoped components and dependencies at the approved depth. Sample a tool or process change and a dated criticality decision linked to safeguards or follow-up. Controls: SA-15, SA-15(3). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g115; first milestone: Collect the approved development process and tool baseline, a reviewed tool change, and a lifecycle criticality analysis and decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G116. Unsupported components need lifecycle decisions and replacement evidence.** Component maintainers and the deployment asset owner reconcile installed versions against dated supplier support commitments. For a sampled unsupported component, retain a verified replacement or an approved alternative support arrangement, its authority, residual risk and review date. Link the deployed inventory, updated support evidence and verification results. Controls: SA-22. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g116; first milestone: Collect current inventory and supplier support dates, and a sampled replacement verification or signed alternative support decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G117. Sovereignty and jurisdiction risk needs an approved sponsor assessment.** The sponsor business owner and designated security, privacy and legal authorities define the assessed business functions, data and jurisdictions. Assess potential injury from external legal compulsion, document jurisdiction-specific threats and vulnerabilities, and update categorization where supported. Retain reviewed risk and treatment decisions for each relevant jurisdiction. Use G111 for separate processing and storage location evidence. Sovereignty: assessments. Controls: SA-400. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g117; first milestone: Collect the scoped injury, threat, vulnerability and jurisdiction risk assessments, plus the signed treatment and categorization decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G118. System and communications protection policy needs assigned ownership and review.** The sponsor system-security lead approves policy and operating procedures for the assessed communications and protection boundary. Name the authority for updates, record the review cadence and triggers, document distribution to assigned roles, and sample an operating procedure followed under the approved policy. Controls: SC-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g118; first milestone: Collect approved policy and procedures, responsible roles, distribution and one dated operating record (Phase 44.1).
- **G119. Management separation and shared-resource isolation need scoped evidence.** Component maintainers and deployment security owners map management functions separately from user functions and inventory shared storage, cache, compute and messaging resources. Document the effective privilege and isolation boundaries. In approved fixtures, verify an ordinary role cannot use the management path and distinct principals do not receive each other’s synthetic data through resource reuse. Controls: SC-2, SC-4. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g119; first milestone: Collect reviewed function and resource boundaries with allowed management and denied cross-role or cross-resource results (Phase 44.1).
- **G120. Availability protections and capacity limits need deployment evidence.** Service operators and maintainers identify applicable denial-of-service scenarios and agree on capacity, bandwidth, redundancy, upstream safeguards and recovery thresholds. From a controlled staging load or resilience exercise, retain configured limits, service and alert timing, failover or recovery observations, and treatment for uncovered paths. Controls: SC-5, SC-5(2). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g120; first milestone: Collect approved availability thresholds and a measured staging load and recovery record (Phase 44.1).
- **G122. Default-deny and allowed incoming communications need effective rule evidence.** Deployment gateway operators and component maintainers approve each default-deny boundary, exception and authorized inbound source and destination pair. Review effective network and service rules and record harmless allowed and denied cases from the assessed layers. Keep evidence for application route decisions separate from evidence for the surrounding gateways and host rules. Controls: SC-7(5), SC-7(11). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g122; first milestone: Collect signed traffic policy and exact settings with allowed and denied ingress and default-rule results (Phase 44.1).
- **G123. Remote tunnel safeguards and authenticated proxy use need operating evidence.** Endpoint, VPN and proxy operators map assessed remote access and outbound flows. Verify prevention of unapproved split tunneling, safeguards and expiry for approved exceptions, and authenticated proxy enforcement for defined destinations. Capture only redacted configurations and authenticated and refused connection results. Record authorized scope decisions where a mechanism is unused. Controls: SC-7(7), SC-7(8). Owner role: owner.
