Tracked as POA&M item g123; first milestone: Collect approved remote networking scope, tunnel and proxy settings, and enforced exception and authentication results (Phase 44.1).
- **G124. Outbound threat denial and responsible-identity auditing need scoped evidence.** Deployment monitoring and egress operators, with component maintainers, approve the outgoing traffic criteria and actor attribution requirement. Use harmless fixtures to verify the measured layer detects and blocks an unapproved outgoing condition and records the responsible identity or approved mapping. Review the path from decision to audit receipt and document gaps for traffic outside that layer. Controls: SC-7(9). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g124; first milestone: Collect approved egress criteria, a benign blocked result and a redacted attributable audit receipt (Phase 44.1).
- **G125. Host boundary protections and security-tool subnet separation need deployment evidence.** Host and network operators inventory the assessed components that require host-based controls and the designated security tools that require physical subnet separation. Collect effective host policies, approved topology and managed interconnect settings. Verify only approved communications across the tool boundary and record an authorized scope decision if physical separation is out of scope. Controls: SC-7(12), SC-7(13). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g125; first milestone: Collect effective host boundary settings and reviewed physical separation and interface verification for designated tool networks (Phase 44.1).
- **G126. Confidentiality and integrity in transit need per-link deployment evidence.** Component maintainers and deployment communications owners map every assessed link, TLS termination, loopback exception and any end-to-end protection layer. Collect effective protocol and trust settings plus accepted and refused peer or integrity results for the selected cryptographic mechanism. Treat built-in TLS and G13 platform attestation as scoped inputs and record explicit inheritance and exceptions. Controls: SC-8, SC-8(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g126; first milestone: Collect assessed flow and termination inventory with configuration and connection verification for each applicable transit protection (Phase 44.1).
- **G127. Connection termination and idle timing need end-to-end evidence.** Deployment service and network operators and component maintainers approve idle limits and normal termination behavior for each assessed connection type. Observe the transport closing on end-of-session and at the effective idle threshold, including intermediate gateways where applicable. Distinguish a closed connection from invalidation of an application token under SC-23. Controls: SC-10. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g127; first milestone: Collect approved inactivity limits, effective service and gateway configurations, and measured transport closure records (Phase 44.1).
- **G128. Key lifecycle and authorized recovery need deployment evidence.** Deployment key custodians and component maintainers inventory assessed key uses and locations and approve generation, agreement, distribution, access, rotation, revocation and retirement. Review an authorized recovery exercise for applicable information after loss of a synthetic user key and prove access remains denied to an unauthorized role. Keep all key material out of evidence and retain X8’s scope for algorithm guidance. Controls: SC-12, SC-12(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g128; first milestone: Collect the approved key lifecycle and custody matrix and redacted rotation, revocation and recovery exercise records (Phase 44.1).
- **G129. Approved cryptography by use and deployed configuration need evidence.** The sponsor cryptographic authority and component maintainers map each assessed use to an approved algorithm, key strength, provider, version and operating mode. Reconcile effective settings with the build inventory and document the required validation or accepted exception with its authority and expiry. Retain X8’s comparable-strength evaluation as an input for its stated scope. Controls: SC-13. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g129; first milestone: Collect the reviewed cryptography-by-use inventory, deployed provider records and required validation references or signed exceptions (Phase 44.1).
- **G130. Collaborative-device activation and restricted-area disablement need evidence.** Endpoint operators and the secure-area owner inventory collaborative cameras, microphones and applications in scope. Review approved remote activation exceptions and the local usage indication. Verify remote activation is refused outside the exceptions and approved devices are disabled or removed in designated secure areas. Record the controlled test and area scope. Controls: SC-15, SC-15(3). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g130; first milestone: Collect approved device and area inventories, activation exception settings, observed usage indicators and restricted-area verification (Phase 44.1).
- **G131. Certificate issuance and approved trust stores need deployment evidence.** Deployment PKI operators and component maintainers inventory assessed certificates, issuing authorities and trust stores. Verify approved issuance, renewal and revocation processes and collect the effective trust-anchor set for each deployment path. Use approved fixture certificates to verify accepted and refused trust decisions. Keep actual private keys out of assessment artifacts. Controls: SC-17. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g131; first milestone: Collect the approved authority and trust-store inventory, issuance and lifecycle sample, and scoped certificate verification results (Phase 44.1).
- **G132. Mobile code acquisition, execution controls and confinement need evidence.** Deployment endpoint owners and component maintainers define acceptable mobile code, its sources and authorized acquisition, development and use. Using benign test artifacts, verify identification and corrective action for prohibited code, prevention of unauthorized download or execution and automatic execution, any required pre-execution approval, and confinement of permitted code in verified VM environments. Record applicability for each assessed mechanism. Controls: SC-18, SC-18(1), SC-18(2), SC-18(3), SC-18(4), SC-18(5). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g132; first milestone: Collect approved mobile-code rules, distribution and enforcement settings, safe denied cases and evidence of the required independent execution boundary (Phase 44.1).
- **G133. Authoritative DNS integrity and delegation evidence need verified scope.** The deployment DNS authority inventories assessed zones, authoritative service providers and delegated child zones. Review the authenticated resolution configuration, retained signatures and parent-child trust evidence for applicable chains. Capture verification of the in-scope resolver view and relevant child-zone status without publishing protected internal names. Controls: SC-20. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g133; first milestone: Collect redacted authoritative zone settings, response verification and parent-child delegation evidence or approved scope treatment (Phase 44.1).
- **G134. Resolver validation, fault tolerance and role separation need evidence.** Deployment DNS operators inventory recursive and caching services, authorized callers and internal and external authoritative roles. Verify that the assessed resolver requests and validates authenticated responses and handles validation failures according to approved policy. Observe a controlled failure or failover and review effective separation of service roles. Controls: SC-21, SC-22. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g134; first milestone: Collect resolver settings and validation results, role and network diagrams, and a scoped DNS resilience exercise record (Phase 44.1).
- **G135. Session authenticity, identifier generation and logout invalidation need evidence.** Component maintainers and deployment identity operators inventory assessed communications sessions and identifier issuers. Review authenticity and approved randomness requirements. Use exact-release test results and controlled deployment observations for distinct system-generated identifiers, rejection of unrecognized identifiers, and denial after logout or termination. G3 contributes only its scoped relay ingress evidence. Controls: SC-23, SC-23(1), SC-23(3). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g135; first milestone: Collect the assessed session map and release and deployment verification of session authenticity, identifier issuance and invalidation (Phase 44.1).
- **G136. Storage confidentiality and integrity need assessed component and media evidence.** Component maintainers and deployment storage and key owners inventory covered information, storage locations and media, including applicable backups and logs. Record approved confidentiality and integrity protections and boundaries of any inherited disk or storage encryption. Verify released sealed-state behavior for its covered data and collect redacted operating configuration and authorized recovery or integrity results for the remaining deployed stores. Controls: SC-28, SC-28(1). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g136; first milestone: Collect an approved information-to-storage protection matrix and scoped cryptographic at-rest test and deployment settings with accepted exceptions (Phase 44.1).
- **G137. Assessed technology diversity needs architecture rationale and operating evidence.** The sponsor architecture owner identifies components for which technology diversity is required and documents the intended risk reduction and correlated dependencies. Compare the approved design to installed component, platform and provider inventories. Use an approved resilience exercise or disposition for gaps in the declared diversity boundary. Controls: SC-29. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g137; first milestone: Collect approved diversity criteria, assessed technology inventory and a reviewed dependency or resilience result (Phase 44.1).
- **G138. Process execution domains need independent boundary evidence.** Deployment runtime operators and component maintainers inventory assessed processes and their execution domains, privileges and shared resources. Review the effective isolation settings at each applicable host, service, container or VM boundary. Verify that distinct synthetic principals cannot read each other’s test process data through reuse of shared resources. Record any dependency on inherited host protection. Controls: SC-39. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g138; first milestone: Collect execution-domain maps, effective isolation configuration and approved separate-domain verification results (Phase 44.1).
- **G139. Clock synchronization needs assessed component settings and drift evidence.** The deployment infrastructure owner inventories time sources and assessed components, approves synchronization and drift requirements, and records the effective settings and exception process. Compare observed offsets across components and verify alert or correction behavior in a controlled test. Use G18 audit timestamp evidence only for its covered log behavior. Controls: SC-45. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g139; first milestone: Collect approved time-source and drift settings, measured component offsets and dated correction or alert evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G140. Awareness and training policy and procedures need approved operating records.** The sponsor training policy official approves the awareness and training scope, procedures, coordination, and accountable security and privacy roles. Verify distribution to required audiences and review at the approved schedule and after applicable changes. Record a dated policy or procedure revision and the resulting operating action. Controls: AT-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g140; first milestone: Collect approved policy and procedures, a named coordinator, distribution and review records, and a sampled corrective action (Phase 44.1).
- **G141. Literacy training and reporting awareness need representative delivery evidence.** The deployment training lead and security and privacy awareness owners approve onboarding, renewal and change-triggered literacy training for staff, managers and contractors. Verify the content teaches recognition and authorized reporting of insider concerns, social engineering and social mining. Retain versioned awareness material, redacted delivery and completion records, and a content revision addressing a reviewed incident lesson. Controls: AT-2, AT-2(2), AT-2(3). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g141; first milestone: Collect approved literacy and reporting modules, a sampled training and awareness delivery record, and a documented revision from incident lessons (Phase 44.1).
- **G142. Role-based training needs a verified link to authorized duties and access.** The sponsor workforce assurance and access owners identify roles and training required before access or assigned duties. Compare sampled eligibility and access approvals with completion dates. Retain the approved refresher schedule, a role-specific exercise and a content update triggered by a system change or applicable incident lesson. Controls: AT-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g142; first milestone: Collect the role and training matrix, redacted pre-access completion and authorization records, and a dated curriculum or refresher review (Phase 44.1).
- **G143. Training record monitoring and retention need operating evidence.** The training records steward establishes monitoring and retention rules for literacy and role-based training. Verify a redacted completion and overdue-training sample against the records repository. Retain evidence of authorized review, follow-up and the configured retention period, and restrict personal training data to approved holders. Controls: AT-4. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g143; first milestone: Collect the retention rule, redacted training extracts, and a sampled overdue item and follow-up record (Phase 44.1).
- **G144. Maintenance policy and procedures need approved scope and operating records.** The sponsor maintenance policy official approves procedures for onsite, offsite and non-local maintenance, assigned roles and coordination with security and privacy authorities. Record assigned ownership, distribution and scheduled or event-triggered review. Sample implementation through an approved maintenance record. Controls: MA-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g144; first milestone: Collect approved policy and procedures, a named coordinator, distribution and revision records, and a sampled maintenance authorization (Phase 44.1).
- **G145. Controlled maintenance needs approval, media handling and post-service verification.** The deployment maintenance manager and component custodian identify assessed items and approved maintenance, repair and replacement rules. Trace a sampled job through scheduling, approval, monitoring and service history. For offsite service, verify the named authority approved removal and required information was sanitized. Verify potentially affected controls after the job and document return or replacement disposition. Controls: MA-2. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g145; first milestone: Collect the maintenance schedule, approved work order and monitoring record, applicable offsite and sanitization receipts, and post-service control checks (Phase 44.1).
- **G146. Maintenance tools and diagnostic media need authorized inventory and inspection evidence.** The deployment maintenance tool custodian and endpoint security lead identify tools and diagnostic media approved for assessed systems. Verify periodic review and observed authorized use, checks for unauthorized changes to tools, and malicious-code screening before use of diagnostic media. Record a sampled approved or refused item with its disposition and link to incident handling when applicable. Controls: MA-3, MA-3(1), MA-3(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g146; first milestone: Collect the tool approval and review register, sampled tool integrity and diagnostic media checks, and the recorded disposition (Phase 44.1).
- **G147. Maintenance equipment removal needs verified information and custody safeguards.** The maintenance facility authority and equipment custodian approve removal rules for assessed equipment. Verify a sampled exit decision using evidence that protected information is absent, the equipment was sanitized or destroyed, or the equipment was retained. If the approved process allows an exception, retain the expressly authorized exemption and custody record. Controls: MA-3(3). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g147; first milestone: Collect the removal policy, a redacted equipment check and a dated release, hold or exception decision with custody evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G148. Non-local maintenance needs monitored authorization and session closure evidence.** The deployment remote maintenance owner and security monitoring lead identify approved tools and diagnostic access in the system plan. Verify approval and strong authentication for a sampled session, retained activity and required audit events, review for anomalous behavior, and termination of the session and its network connections at completion. Controls: MA-4, MA-4(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g148; first milestone: Collect the approved system-plan scope and a redacted session authorization, authentication, audit review and termination record (Phase 44.1).
- **G149. Non-local service needs comparable safeguards and controlled reconnection evidence.** The deployment system security owner and service custodian compare the non-local maintenance environment and tools with the assessed system safeguards. Verify a sampled component was removed and sanitized before service, inspected and sanitized for potentially malicious software afterward, and checked before reconnecting under approved custody and release rules. Controls: MA-4(3). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g149; first milestone: Collect the reviewed safeguards comparison, removal and pre-service sanitization records, and post-service inspection, sanitization and reconnection approval (Phase 44.1).
- **G150. Non-local maintenance session isolation and cryptographic protection need verified configuration.** The deployment access and network security owners approve replay-resistant authenticators, physical or logical separation, and protections for communication confidentiality and integrity. Verify configuration and a permitted maintenance-only session in an approved test environment. Check refusal of invalid or replayed authorization with synthetic data and retain redacted records, with evidence that general sessions cannot use the maintenance path. Controls: MA-4(4), MA-4(6). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g150; first milestone: Collect approved authenticator and communication settings, measured isolation and protection verification, and redacted allowed and refused session results (Phase 44.1).
- **G151. Maintenance personnel authorization and escorted service need verified records.** The maintenance authority and personnel security lead maintain approved personnel and organizations and verify authorization before unescorted service. For a sampled supervised job, record the qualified escort and approval, sanitization of volatile storage and removal or disconnection and custody of non-volatile media. Verify approved alternate controls and their implementation if equipment cannot be sanitized, removed or disconnected. Controls: MA-5, MA-5(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g151; first milestone: Collect the controlled authorization register, a redacted eligibility or escorted service record, and a storage preparation receipt or documented alternate safeguards (Phase 44.1).
- **G152. Maintenance support and spares need verified response commitments.** The deployment service owner identifies critical components, approved support and replacement times, designated providers and spare locations. Reconcile a dated support agreement and spare inventory with the requirements. Sample a completed event or approved exercise and verify elapsed time and escalation for any miss. Controls: MA-6. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g152; first milestone: Collect critical component timing requirements, current support and spare records, and a dated response result and disposition (Phase 44.1).
- **G153. Media protection policy and procedures need approved operating evidence.** The sponsor media protection official approves assessed media scope, accountable custodian roles and procedures for access, marking, storage, movement, use and disposition. Record approval, distribution, review triggers and a sampled operating action that followed the procedures. Controls: MP-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g153; first milestone: Collect approved policy and procedures, named owners, distribution and review records, and one traceable operating action (Phase 44.1).
- **G155. Media marking and secure storage need inventory and facility evidence.** The information owner and media custodian approve marking and controlled storage rules by media type and sensitivity. Verify sampled markings for distribution limits and handling caveats, applicable approved exemption boundaries, and secure physical storage and custody until authorized sanitization or destruction. Controls: MP-3, MP-4. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g155; first milestone: Collect approved marking and storage rules, a redacted media and storage sample, and dated custody or exemption records (Phase 44.1).
- **G156. Media transport outside controlled areas needs verified custody evidence.** The deployment transport authority and media custodian approve routes, protection requirements and personnel for assessed media leaving controlled areas. Sample a shipment or approved exercise through dispatch, custody handoffs, delivery and disposition, with authorization and evidence of the required protection at each handoff. Controls: MP-5. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g156; first milestone: Collect approved transport and personnel rules, a redacted shipment and custody record, and recipient acknowledgement (Phase 44.1).
- **G157. Media sanitization and portable media preparation need verified outcomes.** The deployment media sanitization authority approves methods and verification appropriate to media type and information categorization. Sample sanitized media before disposal, transfer or reuse and trace the authorization, method and successful verification. Verify required non-destructive preparation of portable media before connection on approved non-production specimens, with refusal when preparation is missing. Controls: MP-6, MP-6(3). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g157; first milestone: Collect approved method and verification records, a redacted disposition receipt, and a sampled pre-connection preparation and approval result (Phase 44.1).
- **G158. Remote media purge or wipe needs approved scope and authorized test evidence.** The deployment endpoint management authority documents assessed devices, triggering conditions, authorized roles and strong authentication for purge or wipe. Exercise the procedure on a disposable non-production device containing only synthetic data. Record scoped authorization, denial for an unauthorized role, execution status and independent confirmation of the expected result. Controls: MP-6(8). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g158; first milestone: Collect approved device scope and trigger rules, redacted authorization and refusal results, and verified completion on a disposable test device (Phase 44.1).
- **G159. Media downgrading and public release need reviewed sanitization evidence.** The sponsor information release authority approves assessed media scope, approved downgrading mechanisms and verification matched to sensitivity and recipient authorization. Sample a public-release exercise using synthetic protected markers. Verify that protected information is removed before release, that the authorized recipient or publication scope is recorded, and that failed verification blocks release. Controls: MP-8, MP-8(3). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g159; first milestone: Collect the approved downgrade procedure, a redacted verification and release decision, and a documented refusal when protection checks fail (Phase 44.1).
- **G160. Physical and environmental protection policy requires sponsor approval.** The sponsor physical security official and facility leads document the applicable policy and procedures, recipients, roles, coordination and review events. Capture publication and a dated review. Record provider or landlord responsibilities and submit any inheritance or tailoring decision to the sponsor security authority for review. Controls: PE-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g160; first milestone: Collect policy approval, distribution and a recent policy or procedure review with named facility responsibilities (Phase 44.1).
- **G161. Physical access authorization and identification credentials need evidence.** The sponsor facilities access manager approves zone access, credential and identification card standards. Sample authorization, issuance, periodic list review and removal when access ends. Confirm required identification fields through the approved template or a redacted issuance checklist without collecting staff photographs or badge identifiers. Controls: PE-2, PE-2(400). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g161; first milestone: Collect the zone access roster procedure, approved badge template and redacted issuance, review and removal records (Phase 44.1).
- **G162. Entry enforcement and physical security inspections need site evidence.** The sponsor site security manager designates controlled entry and public boundaries, visitor escort conditions, access device inventories and lost or compromised credential response. Sample authorized access and logs, credential replacement or removal, and a qualified site inspection with authorized follow-up, including changed inspection cadence when required. Record inherited site controls for sponsor validation. Controls: PE-3, PE-3(400). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g162; first milestone: Collect the approved entry plan, redacted access and device lifecycle samples, and an inspection report with corrective action tracking (Phase 44.1).
- **G163. Physical protection of transmission paths and output needs verification.** The sponsor network facilities lead and information custodian identify protected transmission and distribution lines and devices that can display or print in-scope information. Verify access controls on each route type and sample physical controls for output handling by authorized users. Document cases without local output for sponsor tailoring review. Controls: PE-4, PE-5. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g163; first milestone: Collect a controlled route and output inventory, approved safeguards and a representative inspection or output access exercise (Phase 44.1).
- **G164. Physical monitoring and security incident handoff need evidence.** The sponsor physical security operations manager records monitored facilities, intrusion and surveillance coverage, log review triggers and frequency, retention and access restrictions. Sample an alarm or authorized exercise, a dated log review and escalation into organizational incident response. Have privacy officials confirm handling of surveillance records. Controls: PE-6, PE-6(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g164; first milestone: Collect monitoring settings, a dated access-log review and a redacted alarm or incident exercise showing response handoff (Phase 44.1).
- **G165. Visitor records and anomaly escalation need facility evidence.** The sponsor visitor-services lead defines retention, review frequency and anomaly recipients. Sample controlled visitor registration, a dated record review and an anomaly escalation or exercise. Use a restricted evidence reference or redacted record to avoid redisclosing visitor identities. Controls: PE-8. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g165; first milestone: Collect the visitor record procedure, a dated review and a redacted escalation record or exercise result (Phase 44.1).
- **G166. Protected power cabling and emergency shutoff need site verification.** The sponsor facilities electrical lead identifies protected equipment and cabling and reviews emergency isolation coverage, access for authorized responders and protections against unauthorized activation. Use an authorized maintenance inspection and test or approved simulation to verify coverage across in-scope sites. Assess provider-controlled sites through scoped service evidence. Controls: PE-9, PE-10. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g166; first milestone: Collect electrical safeguard inspection records, approved emergency shutoff roles and the latest maintenance test or simulation (Phase 44.1).
- **G167. Backup power and emergency egress lighting need test records.** The sponsor continuity and facilities leads approve the required orderly shutdown or long-term power transfer mode. Collect an authorized power-loss test showing UPS behavior and maintenance records for automatic emergency lighting along exits and evacuation routes. Validate site and provider coverage before accepting inheritance. Controls: PE-11, PE-12. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g167; first milestone: Collect an approved power continuity mode, UPS test and automatic emergency lighting inspection with evacuation route coverage (Phase 44.1).
- **G168. Fire detection, suppression and emergency response need facility evidence.** The sponsor fire safety lead verifies independently powered detection and suppression, automatic notifications to named responders, qualified inspections at approved intervals and timely remediation. Review site safeguarding decisions against firefighting water capacity and emergency response assumptions. Assess landlord or provider evidence for each covered site. Controls: PE-13, PE-13(1), PE-13(4), PE-13(400). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g168; first milestone: Collect fire system test records, notification exercise, inspection and deficiency follow-up, and documented emergency service assumptions (Phase 44.1).
- **G169. Environmental monitoring and water isolation need facility evidence.** The sponsor building operations lead approves applicable environmental thresholds and monitoring intervals. Review a representative monitoring trend or alert and confirm water shutoff or isolation valves are accessible, operational and known to responsible staff. Document any provider inheritance by location for sponsor review. Controls: PE-14, PE-15. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g169; first milestone: Collect approved thresholds, representative monitoring evidence, and valve inspection or test with staff acknowledgement (Phase 44.1).
- **G170. Facility delivery and removal authorization needs movement records.** The sponsor asset custodian defines controlled component classes and who authorizes receipt or removal. Sample entry, release and custody reconciliation against asset records. Use restricted references or redact identifying information while retaining dates, approvals and exceptions needed for assessment. Controls: PE-16. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g170; first milestone: Collect the component movement procedure and authorized receipt and removal samples traceable to custody records (Phase 44.1).
- **G171. Alternate work and domestic telework safeguards need sponsor assessment.** The sponsor remote-work authority and physical security lead define approved work sites and information categories. Review site safeguards, incident contacts, approved devices and storage for physical information and assets against departmental requirements and applicable RCMP guidance. Sample an authorized site assessment and evidence of control effectiveness without publishing residential details. Controls: PE-17, PE-400, PE-400(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g171; first milestone: Collect approved alternate-site criteria and a sanitized effectiveness assessment covering devices, physical storage and incident contact (Phase 44.1).
- **G172. International telework exceptions need sponsor decisions.** The sponsor international telework authority establishes exceptional access criteria and identifies the applicable departmental approval officials. Where use is permitted, sample a time-limited request with location and personnel risk assessment, security briefing, approvals and end-of-access evidence. Where prohibited or outside scope, submit the policy and deployment boundary to the assessor for review. Controls: PE-400(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g172; first milestone: Collect the approved restriction and one sanitized exception decision with risk assessment and expiry, or documented prohibited-use scope (Phase 44.1).
- **G173. Security operations centre coverage needs sponsor validation.** The sponsor security operations authority identifies the physical and technical monitoring coverage, operators and escalation responsibility for in-scope services and facilities. Review any shared or provider service claim against its scope and verify an observed exercise or incident handoff. Submit residual coverage decisions for sponsor review. Controls: PE-401. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g173; first milestone: Collect an approved monitoring coverage and responsibility map tied to a representative exercise or incident handoff (Phase 44.1).
- **G174. Personnel security policy requires sponsor approval.** The sponsor personnel security official defines policy scope, accountable roles, procedures, recipients, review intervals and update triggers. Record approval, distribution and recent review. Confirm the applicable boundary for employee and external personnel procedures with sponsor security and privacy officials. Controls: PS-1. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g174; first milestone: Collect the approved personnel security policy, role assignments, dissemination record and dated procedure review (Phase 44.1).
- **G175. Position screening requirements and personnel eligibility need evidence.** The sponsor personnel security and human resources leads define screening criteria by position, review cadence and rescreening triggers, and maintain position descriptions with security and privacy duties. Sample an eligibility determination before access and a rescreening or due-date review using redacted workflow evidence without background investigation contents. Controls: PS-2, PS-3, PS-9. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g175; first milestone: Collect the position screening matrix, approved role description and redacted screening-before-access and rescreening samples (Phase 44.1).
- **G176. Termination and credential revocation need timestamped sponsor evidence.** The sponsor human resources, identity and asset leads define termination notification, access disablement deadline, credential revocation, exit topics and asset recovery. Sample a termination or authorized exercise against the deadline and verify reassignment or retained access to organizational information. Record inherited directory actions at their assessed boundary. Controls: PS-4. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g176; first milestone: Collect a redacted termination workflow with access timestamps, credential and asset recovery and transfer of organizational information (Phase 44.1).
- **G177. Access agreements need documented issuance and renewal.** The sponsor access governance lead and privacy office approve agreement versions, review intervals and re-signing triggers. Sample a recorded acceptance before access and a renewal after a revision or scheduled interval. Retain a restricted reference or redacted evidence for assessor review. Controls: PS-6. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g177; first milestone: Collect approved agreement versions, review history and redacted before-access acceptance and renewal records (Phase 44.1).
- **G178. External personnel screening and provider notification need sponsor evidence.** The sponsor procurement and personnel security officials document external personnel screening, provider obligations, government oversight and end-user responsibilities, notification recipients and deadlines for transfers or terminations. Sample sponsor oversight and a timely credential or privilege change under the applicable agreement. Record provider scope and submit inheritance decisions for review. Controls: PS-7. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g178; first milestone: Collect approved external personnel obligations and a redacted screening, notification or access change and provider oversight sample (Phase 44.1).
- **G179. Personnel sanctions and timely notification need sponsor evidence.** The sponsor human resources and security officials approve a formal sanctions procedure for security and privacy violations, notification recipients and timing. Provide a restricted evidence reference or sanitized exercise showing initiation, authorized notification and oversight without circulating identities or case details. Controls: PS-8. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g179; first milestone: Collect the approved sanctions and notification procedure with a dated sanitized evidence reference or exercise (Phase 44.1).
- **G180. Security program leadership and authorized investment need records.** The sponsor security executive and investment authority approve the organization-wide security program plan and its distribution. Document appointment, responsibilities, resources and authority, and trace required security and privacy funding or approved exceptions to planning and investment records. Controls: PM-1, PM-2, PM-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g180; first milestone: Collect approved program plan and distribution, accountable appointment and a sampled resourcing decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G181. Program remediation and monitoring need verified review records.** The sponsor program assurance lead approves POA&M reporting and prioritization, performance measures, and the testing, training and continuous monitoring plans. Sample coordinated results, program-level reporting to designated recipients, approved remediation or escalation and later review of effectiveness. Controls: PM-4, PM-6, PM-14, PM-31. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g181; first milestone: Collect approved reporting cadence and plans, performance results and a sampled finding through follow-up (Phase 44.1).
- **G182. System and personal information inventories need approved coverage.** The enterprise inventory and privacy leads reconcile in-scope systems and programs with the applications, projects and systems processing personal information. Record each custodian, update cadence, change trigger and an affected inventory entry. Retain only approved references to personal information. Controls: PM-5, PM-5(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g182; first milestone: Collect reviewed system and personal-information inventory coverage and a sampled change and review record (Phase 44.1).
- **G183. Enterprise architecture and mission use need traceability to approved purpose.** The enterprise architect and business owners map essential processes and authorized uses to systems, data flows and safeguards. Identify nonessential functions selected for offloading, record destination responsibilities and risks, and sample operating use against approved purposes. Record treatment or signed scope determination for omissions. Controls: PM-7, PM-7(1), PM-11, PM-32. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g183; first milestone: Collect approved architecture and mission mapping, scoped offload decisions and a sampled authorized-purpose review (Phase 44.1).
- **G184. Critical infrastructure protection plan needs approved security and privacy scope.** The sponsor critical infrastructure authority approves the protection plan and identifies key resources, dependencies, security and privacy safeguards, coordination arrangements and update triggers. Retain applicable approval, review and exercise records or an authorized scope decision. Controls: PM-8. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g184; first milestone: Collect the protected infrastructure scope, approved plan, designated team and reviewed exercise or applicability decision (Phase 44.1).
- **G185. Enterprise risk framing and authorization governance need accountable decisions.** The sponsor risk executive documents authorized assumptions, constraints, tolerances and trade-offs, with named risk and authorization roles. Approve the strategy and processes across assessed environments, and sample an actual authorization or risk treatment that records decision grounds, review triggers and authority. Controls: PM-9, PM-10, PM-28, PM-29. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g185; first milestone: Collect approved strategy and framing, appointments, and a sampled authorization or risk treatment record (Phase 44.1).
- **G186. Insider response team and workforce development need role and operating evidence.** The sponsor security, privacy and personnel leads approve the cross-disciplinary insider handling team and applicable referral, privacy and escalation procedures. Approve workforce competency and development planning and collect redacted training, exercise or staffing records with follow-up. Controls: PM-12, PM-13. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g186; first milestone: Collect authorized cross-disciplinary team and referral procedure, an exercise receipt and workforce development review (Phase 44.1).
- **G187. Threat awareness and external community participation need approved sharing evidence.** The sponsor threat, privacy and external liaison leads approve participating associations, authorized recipients and sharing rules. Exercise a sanitized threat awareness handoff and the approved automated route, verify restrictions and receipt, and document subsequent review or response. Controls: PM-15, PM-16, PM-16(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g187; first milestone: Collect designated participant and sharing decisions, operating contact evidence and redacted automated receipt and response (Phase 44.1).
- **G188. Outsourced controlled information needs verified protection authority.** The sponsor procurement, information and contracting authorities identify outsourced services that handle controlled information. Record approved protection terms, processor boundaries and responsibilities, evidence review and any signed applicable authorization. Sample a reviewed supplier arrangement and retained safeguard evidence. Controls: PM-17. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g188; first milestone: Collect approved outsourcing policy and a scoped supplier agreement with safeguard and approval evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G189. Privacy program ownership and reporting need approved governance evidence.** The sponsor privacy executive approves and distributes the organizational program plan, records delegated authority and resources, and approves reporting content, recipients and cadence. Retain a dated privacy accountability report, its review and approved delivery evidence. Controls: PM-18, PM-19, PM-27. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g189; first milestone: Collect the approved privacy plan and appointment, plus a sampled reviewed report and dissemination record (Phase 44.1).
- **G190. Public privacy information and the complaints route need operating evidence.** The sponsor privacy communications and complaints leads maintain public resource and notice inventory for applicable digital services, approve current notices and accessible contact paths, and test a harmless enquiry through intake, tracking and response with restricted case records. Controls: PM-20, PM-20(1), PM-26. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g190; first milestone: Collect dated public notices and resource links, approval and review records, and a redacted request-to-response receipt (Phase 44.1).
- **G191. Privacy disclosure and information quality procedures need reviewed records.** The sponsor disclosure and information quality authorities approve rules for required disclosures and authorized corrections. Use protected records to demonstrate dates, required recipients and reasons for disclosure, and sample a quality review or correction with approved outcome. Retain only redacted references for assessment. Controls: PM-21, PM-22. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g191; first milestone: Collect approved procedures, a reviewed disclosure record and a dated accuracy or correction sample (Phase 44.1).
- **G192. Data governance, matching review and personal information minimization need scope evidence.** The sponsor data and privacy leads document committee membership, authority and reviewed decisions. Where matching is in scope, obtain the authorized board review and periodic assessment. Show minimization for testing, training and research through approved synthetic or de-identified dataset controls and exception records. Record authorized applicability decisions. Controls: PM-23, PM-24, PM-25. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g192; first milestone: Collect committee or board authority, applicable matching review and a sampled minimized-data approval (Phase 44.1).
- **G193. Program supply-chain strategy and critical supplier review need authorized records.** The sponsor supply chain executive and procurement lead approve enterprise strategy through acquisition, operation, maintenance and disposal. Identify critical suppliers and dependencies, prioritize by mission impact, and sample due diligence, residual risk, assigned treatment and recurring review. Controls: PM-30, PM-30(1). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g193; first milestone: Collect the approved strategy, critical supplier priority register and a sampled supplier risk review and treatment (Phase 44.1).
- **G225. Supplementary account lifecycle needs sponsor evidence.** The sponsor identity governance lead and system owner approve account types, user and role memberships, intended use, authorization and monitoring. Verify expiry, inactivity, orphaned accounts, policy violations and significant risk triggers. Sample approvals, privilege changes, disablement, notices for changes in employment or need, and a required logout outcome. Record the applicable ITSP.10.171 deployment boundary. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.01. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g225; first milestone: Collect approved account lifecycle criteria and redacted provisioning, reviewed use, timed notice or disablement and logout evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G226. Authorized logical access needs deployment enforcement evidence.** The sponsor system and resource owners approve logical access to assessed information and resources, including identities or groups and allowed operations. Demonstrate authorized and denied operations using representative test identities and cite the governing policy and resource boundary. Record applicable scope for ITSP.10.171. Treat mapped base-profile evidence as supporting material until checked against the deployment. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.02. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g226; first milestone: Collect approved access rules and a redacted permission check showing permitted and refused operations on assessed information and resources (Phase 44.1).
- **G227. Information flow approvals and enforcement need deployed evidence.** The sponsor data owner and network security lead approve internal and intersystem flows for the specified information categories. Trace representative approved and denied flows through assessed enforcement points. Referenced product records may help establish the path, while sponsor confirms the assessed routing boundary and inherited rules. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.03. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g227; first milestone: Collect the approved flow matrix, boundary diagram and a representative allowed and denied flow with enforcement records (Phase 44.1).
- **G228. Separation of duties needs authorized role and access evidence.** The sponsor access governance and business process owners identify duties that must be separated and assign corresponding access authorization. Sample assigned users and a conflicting role request or workflow exercise to verify that access supports the separation. Record any approved exception and its scope for assessment. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.04. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g228; first milestone: Collect the approved incompatible duties and role matrix, plus reviewed role assignments or a conflicting request outcome (Phase 44.1).
- **G229. Least privilege and privileged operations need sponsor verification.** The sponsor identity and privileged access leads define minimum task access for users and delegated processes, authorized security functions and privileged roles. Review representative rights and reassignment or removal. Verify separate ordinary accounts, dedicated isolated administrative workstations for privileged actions, denied privileged functions for standard accounts, and logged authorized execution. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.05, ITSP171-03.01.06, ITSP171-03.01.07. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g229; first milestone: Collect the role review and a change record, administrative workstation and ordinary account evidence, and a redacted permitted, denied and logged function sample (Phase 44.1).
- **G230. Failed logon limits and automatic responses need a test result.** The sponsor authentication owner approves the observation window, consecutive failure limit and automatic response, including any unlock or delay criteria. Exercise a representative sign-in route through threshold and recovery with a controlled account. Record inherited service policy and prove it covers the assessed route before accepting it. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.08. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g230; first milestone: Collect authentication settings and timestamped threshold, response and recovery test evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G231. Pre-access system use notices need sponsor approval and display evidence.** The sponsor privacy and system owners approve notice text covering security and privacy rules for specified information. Demonstrate that the assessed human access routes display the notice before granting access. Record where routes have no direct human sign-in and submit that scope decision for assessor review. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.09. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g231; first milestone: Collect approved notice text and timestamped or captured pre-access display evidence for the assessed routes (Phase 44.1).
- **G232. Device lock and session termination need distinct test evidence.** The sponsor endpoint and session service owners approve device lock timing or manual lock requirements, renewed authentication, screen concealment and automatic session disconnect triggers. Test lock and unlock on an assessed device and separately demonstrate session termination on a specified trigger. Record provider or platform inheritance for sponsor approval. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.10, ITSP171-03.01.11. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g232; first milestone: Collect approved endpoint and session policies and distinct demonstrations of display concealment, reauthentication and automatic session termination (Phase 44.1).
- **G233. Remote access routes and privileged remote actions need authorization evidence.** The sponsor remote access and security operations leads inventory each remote access type, approve connection and configuration requirements, and route connections through managed control points. Separately verify permissions for remote privileged commands and security-relevant information. Sample a permitted and denied route or action and document inherited control points for review. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.12. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g233; first milestone: Collect remote access type approvals, an assessed routing and control-point record, and privileged remote action authorization or refusal evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G234. Wireless and mobile access need approved configurations and separate checks.** The sponsor network and endpoint owners approve connection types and configuration for wireless and mobile access before connection. Verify wireless authentication and encryption and that unused radios are disabled before issue or deployment. Sample authorized mobile enrollment and full-device or container encryption for specified information, with a denied or quarantined unapproved connection where practical. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.16, ITSP171-03.01.18. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g234; first milestone: Collect wireless and mobile authorization records, secure wireless configuration and a disabled radio sample, plus mobile enrollment and encryption evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G235. External system use needs approved scope, terms and verification.** The sponsor information and service owners record prohibited and specifically authorized external uses, applicable requirements from security and privacy plans, and approved connection or processing agreements. Sample verification before use of a permitted system and verify restrictions on organization-controlled portable storage there. Record the assessed ITSP.10.171 boundary. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.20. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g235; first milestone: Collect the approved external system inventory, terms and agreement, a dated verification result and applicable portable storage restrictions (Phase 44.1).
- **G236. Public publishing training, review and removal need sponsor evidence.** The sponsor public communications and information owners identify authorized publishers and train them to keep specified information out of public content. Sample a periodic review and a removal or controlled exercise if information is discovered. Record deployment scope for ITSP.10.171 and submit any no-public-content boundary for review. Controls: ITSP171-03.01.22. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g236; first milestone: Collect a publisher training record, recent public content review and a documented removal procedure with case or exercise evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G237. Security literacy and role-based training need deployment records.** The sponsor security and privacy training leads establish initial and recurring literacy that covers insider threat, social engineering and social mining. Set role-specific training before access or duties and at reviewed intervals. Track refresh after system or event changes and revisions to both training streams. Use de-identified learner evidence. Controls: ITSP171-03.02.01, ITSP171-03.02.02. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g237; first milestone: Collect approved curricula and cadence, redacted initial and recurring completion records, and a before-access or before-duty role training sample (Phase 44.1).
- **G238. Selected audit events, record content and retention need verification.** The sponsor logging and records owners select and periodically review logged event types. Verify generation with event type, time, place, source, outcome and affected identities or entities, plus any approved additional data. Sample retention settings and available logs against the approved records schedule. Document any product-only or provider-only scope limits. Controls: ITSP171-03.03.01, ITSP171-03.03.02, ITSP171-03.03.03. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g238; first milestone: Collect the reviewed event list, representative generated records covering required fields and evidence of retention against the approved schedule (Phase 44.1).
- **G239. Audit logging failure alerts and response need exercise evidence.** The sponsor monitoring and service owners set notification recipients, response time and additional action when logging fails. Use an authorized simulation or a sanitized incident reference to demonstrate detection, timely alert, response and recovery. Confirm which failure modes and components are assessed. Controls: ITSP171-03.03.04. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g239; first milestone: Collect the approved logging outage response and timestamped detection, recipient notification and response evidence (Phase 44.1).
- **G240. Audit review, correlation and reporting need operational evidence.** The sponsor security operations lead sets review frequency, criteria for unusual activity and impact, findings recipients and repositories to correlate. Sample a dated review linking records from more than one assessed repository to findings and their reporting. Identify unmonitored sources or provider dependencies for review. Controls: ITSP171-03.03.05. Owner role: owner. The defaults are 7 days for Protected A, 72 hours for Protected B and 24 hours for any classified level. Your organization's authorizing official accepts the lag for each level. Controls: AC-2, IA-5, IA-5(2). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g369; first milestone: Edges refuse credentials whose status list is older than the level allows (Phase 71).

- **G427. People's identities are made but not yet published, and computers cannot be bound yet.** People's identities are made by their own backend at first sign-in, but three parts are not in service yet (Phase 71, 71-10). First, each person's identity log reaches your organization's server only through that person's first session with it, which needs Phase 33's hosted session keys (33-21 to 33-23); until they are on main the logs stay in each person's own secret store, so no check can find a person's identity on the server. Second, the site does not set STERLING\_DID\_DOMAIN for the workbench yet, so a hosted session makes no identity at all; the site chart must render it (Phase 47's site values). Third, binding a computer takes its status list places from the person's own computer slots (D-25, at most 5), which needs your organization's status lists in the session (G465); until then it is refused with a plain sentence. Close each when its dependency lands, and test the post against the real server then. Controls: IA-2, IA-4, IA-5. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 71.

Multi-node audit snapshots need a shared volume on the encrypted class, not yet shown.** A site with more than one OpenSearch node puts its audit and log snapshots on one ReadWriteMany volume (PVC opensearch-snapshots, deploy/values/opensearch.yaml, 47-24), which Longhorn serves through its share manager. Whether a ReadWriteMany volume works on the encrypted storage class, and survives a node loss with its recurring backups, has not been checked: the 47-24 proof ran one OpenSearch node in a container. Check it on Phase 48's multi-node lab-full rig (three OpenSearch nodes writing one repository, a restore from it, and the Longhorn backup of the share), and record the result on the register entry. Controls: CP-9, CP-10. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 48.
- **G449. Guest accounts stay off until a release includes the credential issuing and revocation card (71-12).** Guest accounts (deploy/keycloak/guests.mjs, 47-19) hold lifecycle attributes only: how a guest serves, their organization, access agreement and visit clearance are credentials the security contact issues to the guest in their own session, and an early end files a revocation request that only 71-12's revocation card shows to the issuing officers. 71-12 is now in the release, but its card is not reachable in a hosted session until G465 closes, so guests.mjs keeps CREDENTIAL\_CARD\_REACHABLE false and a site must keep guests off (guests.maxDays 0 or absent in the realm site file) until it runs a release that includes 71-12: the example ships maxDays 0, and guests.mjs create and extend refuse a nonzero maxDays while the release has no credential-issuers policy (71-12's); 47-20, the automatic end, waits on it too. Close this when G465 is closed, CREDENTIAL\_CARD\_REACHABLE is set, and the lab run shows a guest's credentials issued and an early end's request revoked. Controls: AC-2, IA-8. - **G461. Classification thresholds, the system-high, markings, code words and guide rules are your organization's to set.** Nothing ships as values (70.1 D-07): a level with no threshold has no automatic model raise, a section with no systemHigh gives no possible-spill outcome, and no marking pattern, code word or guide rule is built in. Your organization's security officer sets the cost ratios and recall targets per level, the system-high of each deployment layer, the English and French banner and portion markings, the code-word list (labelled at its own level) and the guide and compilation rules from your organization's security classification guide, signed in the classification@1 section. Phase 74.3 documents how. Source: 70.1-CONTEXT.md D-07, D-13, D-16. Controls: AC-16. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g461; first milestone: The operator guide says how your organization's security officer sets thresholds, the system-high, markings, code words and guide rules (Phase 74.3).
- **G465. Credential issuance is built but not yet reachable in a hosted session.** Issuing, revoking and suspending credentials from an officer's own session are built and tested against fakes (Phase 71, 71-12), but a hosted session cannot use them yet, for four reasons. First, the session has no copy of your organization's credential rules: the issuer service and the inbox pickup read them from the hosted trust source of 71-13, which is not on main, so issuing refuses with a plain sentence and inbox items wait. Second, status lists are read from and put on your organization's server only through the officer's hub session, which needs Phase 33's hosted session keys (33-21 to 33-23). Third, the site does not set STERLING\_STATUS\_LIST\_KEY (status-list-\<siteName\>) or STERLING\_OPENBAO\_ISSUER\_ROLE for the workbench yet, and no site file names its credentialIssuers; Phase 47's site values must render both and the key ceremony runbook must name the officers. Fourth, the person's backend moves checked credentials into their own wallet folder in OpenBao (kv/users/\<entity\>/credentials-wallet/), which the extension's Wallet does not read yet; 71-13 joins the two. Close each when its dependency lands, and test issuance end to end against a real OpenBao and hub then. Controls: IA-5, SC-12, SC-17. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 71.
- **G470. Webview pages on a hosted site are unproven: wildcard DNS, certificate, ingress routing and sign-in cookie.** The workbench shows the bundled extension's Chat, Team Studio, Agent Activity and Governance pages in webviews, each from its own origin \<uuid\>.webview.\<instance\>.\<domain\> (Theia's default pattern). The sterling-sessions AppDefinition lists the prefix \*.webview. (ingressHostnamePrefixes) and the theia-cloud release gives the instances Ingress that wildcard host as a rule and as a name on its site-pki certificate (hosts.allWildcardInstances); deploy/test/render-sessions.test.mjs checks the three agree. On a real site, prove the rest and record it: the wildcard DNS record from deploy/runbooks/site-install.md resolves to HAProxy; cert-manager's ws-cert-secret carries the wildcard name from OpenBao's ingress role (allow\_subdomains, with OpenBao's default that allows wildcard names); HAProxy routes the wildcard host and strips each session's path; the operator adds each session's path under the wildcard host; oauth2-proxy's cookie (domain \<instance\>.\<domain\>) reaches the webview host, so no sign-in redirect starts inside a frame; and Chat and Team Studio load in a signed-in session. Also check whether a bundle update (helm upgrade) adds the wildcard host on a site installed before it, as upstream says a change to allWildcardInstances needs the chart reinstalled; if not, add the reinstall to deploy/runbooks/bundle-update.md. Wildcard certificates are discouraged when their scope is wide (a stolen key covers every name under it); this one covers only the webview names, which HAProxy routes to the same session backends as the session host, behind the same sign-in. Describe the scope in the hosted system description (SC-17) and get your organization's PKI authority and the assessor to accept it. If policy refuses wildcard names, the alternatives are a single fixed webview host through THEIA\_WEBVIEW\_EXTERNAL\_ENDPOINT (one name, no wildcard, but the webviews then share one origin and Theia warns about the changed pattern at every start) or per-session certificates, which Theia Cloud 1.2.0's shared instances Ingress does not support. Controls: SC-17, SC-12, SC-23. Owner role: owner. Planned in Phase 48.1.

The workbench container suite writes no evidence report.** The workbench container suite (npm run test:container in the workbench job and the release image job) checks the running image: its UBI 9 base, its non-root user, its Node major, its health and that it makes no outbound connection outside its allow list. It writes no test report, so none of those results can be an evidence rule. The daily off-site copy has no tooling yet.** Owner decision d (D-81) requires a daily copy of the Longhorn backup target and the write-once audit archive to a write-once store at your organization's second site, and the backup runbook describes a sterling-offsite CronJob and offsite.mjs pack and verify for it. No site declares its facility country, operator, administrator screening, hardware or backup location.** Software cannot prove where a facility is, who operates it or what hardware it holds. Phase 48.4 adds the signed site sovereignty declaration (sterling-site-sovereignty/1): the facility country and province, the operator and its jurisdiction, the administrator screening reference, the hardware inventory with its supply chain integrity review, the HSM model and its CMVP certificate, and the countries of the backups and the off-site copy, signed with an operator key your site trust document names and declared again at least every 180 days. ### Does not block production {#protected-a-does-not-block}

- **G398. Observers have no documented releasability vocabulary, agreements or rules of behaviour.** Document the releasability tokens and who sets them, the credentials and agreements an observer needs by sensitivity, and the observer rules of behaviour, then add hub and workbench statements once the release check is on main (48.1-05, 48.1-19). Controls: AC-21, AC-21(400), AC-21(401), AC-16, PS-6, PL-4. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 48.1.
- **G426. The sync hub's trust routes take first copies on trust and check evidence only where they can read.** Three limits of the sync hub as your organization's trust host (Phase 71, 71-09). First, an address for an identity log is first come, first served: a member could post a log for someone else's address before that person does, which blocks that person there until an administrator clears it; people's addresses end in a random id, so the address must be known in advance. Second, a hub that holds no copy of a status list takes the first copy at any version, so a hub started empty (not restored from its backup) could be given an old list by a member before an officer publishes the current one. Third, the hub checks cited evidence only on entries it can open (the project's base part); entries in other cells are checked by the people who read them. Close the first two by having the officer's backend publish each person's log and the current lists when the hub is set up (71-10, 71-12), and record the third in SECURITY.md (71-14). Controls: AC-3, SI-7. Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 71.
- **G463. Portion markings such as (S) match only as bare tokens.** The owner-confirmed marking pattern grammar of classification@1 (2026-11-25) is plain words: letters and digits, single spaces, - and /. A portion marking written (S) is therefore listed as the bare token S, which also matches any standalone capital S and can over-raise (the safe direction, which still costs people time). Decide with the owner whether a classification@2 marking pattern may carry the brackets of a portion marking, and until then list only portion tokens your organization's texts do not use as words. Source: 70.1-04 SUMMARY. Controls: AC-16. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g463; first milestone: The owner decides whether a classification@2 marking pattern may carry portion-marking brackets (Phase 74.3).
- **G464. The classification engine sees only the hidden parts its caller extracts.** assess() reads the visible text and the hidden parts it is given; white-on-white text, tiny fonts, PDF layers and office document metadata reach it only if the caller extracts them. Phase 74.3-03 extracts plain text, Markdown (HTML comments, zero-width text, image alt text, front matter) and staff product documents with their comments; ingested files of other formats are Phase 93's. Source: 70.1-CONTEXT.md D-19; research 3.6. Controls: SI-10, AC-16. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g464; first milestone: The runner extracts hidden parts of plain text, Markdown and staff product documents (Phase 74.3).
- **G479. Vulnerability findings are shown but SI-2 remediation timeliness is not judged from them.** The Compliance view shows the release scan and site rescans with their counts and fixes, but SI-2 remediation timeliness is not judged from the findings. A later phase adds a rule on fixable critical and high findings older than your organization's remediation time. Source: .planning/phases/48.2-live-compliance-evidence-in-the-workbench/48.2-CONTEXT.md (D-29). Controls: SI-2, RA-5. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g479; first milestone: A rule judges fixable critical and high findings older than your organization's remediation time (by 2027-05-31).
- **G529. Resources and exchanges record no supplier, supplier jurisdiction, operator jurisdiction or location.** compliance/resources.json gains supplier and supplierJurisdiction for every entry, and compliance/hosted/exchanges.json gains operatorJurisdiction and location for every exchange, with unknown allowed and shown as Unknown (48.4-02, 48.4-03). The values come from each component's SBOM supplier and its publisher's pages, each with the date read. Sovereignty: data-travels, software, switch-off, outside-laws. Controls: CM-8, SA-9, SA-400(2), SA-400(8). Owner role: maintainers. Planned in Phase 48.4.
- **G534. Supplier's control: a US parent, so the supplier is subject to foreign compulsion.** Recorded by the owner on 2026-11-25: Sterling Computers Canada, ULC is incorporated in Canada and, since a tax reorganization, wholly US-controlled: 99% is held by Sterling North Technologies, which Sterling Computers Corporation (US) owns outright, and 1% by a holding company owned by an individual; neither holding company has staff or property, and all operations sit in Sterling Computers Canada, ULC and Sterling Computers Corporation. Before the reorganization it was wholly owned by Sterling MSP, itself wholly owned by Sterling Computers Corporation. The supplier's jurisdiction is Canada, a Canadian corporation, which the sovereignty card shows as Met; this row is about control. Through its US parent the supplier is subject to foreign compulsion (SA-400(7)), and SA-400(9), arrangements under Canadian public ownership for the life of the system, is not met for the supplier. The exposure is real and can only be mitigated: no supplier access to any site (47 D-01), air-gapped operation, keys your organization holds (KM-3), signed intake and builds from approved inputs at your organization's HQ (48.3), a reproducible-build check (48.3, once run), and source held by a Canadian escrow agent, which the owner has left to be determined (O6, 2026-11-25), so it shows as planned. The card shows each mitigation as active only when its evidence exists, and as planned until then. The sovereignty card shows "Supplier's control: US parent" as Partly met with these mitigations and notes that Sterling holds no client data, keys or site access. Your organization's authorizing official decides whether to accept the residual risk. Foreign ownership, control or influence under PSPC's Contract Security Program sits with the owner's counsel. Sovereignty: switch-off, outside-laws. Controls: SA-400(7), SA-400(9). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g534; first milestone: The ownership structure is recorded and the card shows the supplier's jurisdiction (Canada, Met) and control (US parent, Partly met) with its mitigations (48.4-04, 48.4-05) (Phase 48.4).

## From Protected B {#protected-b}

These matter from Protected B, where validated cryptography and hardened base images are expected.

### Blocks production {#protected-b-blocks}

No timestamp authority dates our signatures.** Our signatures carry no trusted time (the cosign signing configuration is empty), so after a key compromise no signature can be dated before it and every signed item is re-issued. Controls: SI-7, AU-9, CA-7. Owner role: owner. Controls: SA-9(8), SA-400(6). Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g532; first milestone: An attested model server of your organization's at a site declared in Canada (Phase 74.2).
- **G533. No supply chain integrity review is recorded for any hardware model.** No Canadian-made general-purpose CPU or GPU exists at scale, so hardware is judged by a supply chain integrity review of each hardware model (the ITSAP.10.071 criteria) plus site isolation, never by the country of manufacture (48.4 D-05). Your organization reviews each hardware model it runs, the lab's AMD Strix Halo and NVIDIA GB10 first, and cites the review in the site sovereignty declaration. Sovereignty: hardware. Controls: SA-400(8), SR-6. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g533; first milestone: The lab site's hardware models are reviewed and cited in its site sovereignty declaration (by 2027-05-31).
- **G535. The SA-400 enhancements are not selected or assessed for the hosted levels.** The Medium profile selects SA-400 without its nine enhancements, which are the clearest Canadian statement of what sovereign means, and the sovereignty card uses them as its criteria. The owner decided on 2026-11-25 (O4) that hosted Protected B selects SA-400(3) to SA-400(9) as organization-defined additions; 48.4-15 adds their statements and evidence rules from the same facts the card reads, and SA-400(1) and SA-400(2) stay your organization's assessments. Sovereignty: assessments. Controls: SA-400(1), SA-400(2), SA-400(3), SA-400(4), SA-400(5), SA-400(6), SA-400(7), SA-400(8), SA-400(9). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g535; first milestone: Hosted Protected B selects SA-400(3) to SA-400(9) (O4, accepted 2026-11-25) and 48.4-15 adds their statements (Phase 48.4).
- **G536. No independent sovereignty assessment exists; the sovereignty card is a self-check from evidence.** Every credible sovereignty label is issued by an assessor at a stated assurance level (CAN/DGSI 100-8 and its SovereignReady programme; the EU framework's assurance levels). The sovereignty card is a self-check from evidence and says so. The owner decided on 2026-11-25 (O5) to seek a CAN/DGSI 100-8 SovereignReady review once the lab site's rows reach Met; the card's scope line then names that assessment and its level. Sovereignty: assessments. Controls: CA-2, SA-400. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g536; first milestone: The owner seeks a CAN/DGSI 100-8 SovereignReady review once the lab site's rows reach Met (O5, accepted 2026-11-25) (by 2027-05-31).

## From Protected C {#protected-c}

These matter from Protected C.

### Does not block production {#protected-c-does-not-block}

- **G348. ML-KEM-768 is listed only up to Protected B.** The post-quantum cell key wrap uses ML-KEM-768 with P-256, which ITSP.40.111 lists up to Protected B. Above that, ask the Cyber Centre for advice through your organization's sponsor, then build wrap version 3 (ML-KEM-1024 with P-384, feature wrap@3). Until then readers refuse version 3 as not supported yet. Controls: SC-12, SC-13. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g348; first milestone: Wrap version 3 and wrap@3 are reserved, and readers refuse them as not supported yet (Phase 33.2).

## From Confidential {#confidential}

These matter once a site holds classified information, starting at Confidential.

### Does not block production {#confidential-does-not-block}

- **G371. Classified edges need a status list signed every day.** An edge holding classified data accepts only a status list signed in the last 24 hours, even when nothing changed. Every list signature needs an officer's passkey step-up, so a security officer must sign again at least daily for such edges. Your organization plans that duty, with a backup officer, before a classified edge goes live. Controls: AC-2, IA-5. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g371; first milestone: Status lists are signed with the officer's step-up (Phase 71).
- **G415. Nemotron 3 was post-trained on outputs of models from the People's Republic of China.** NVIDIA trained Nemotron 3 from scratch, but part of its post-training data came from DeepSeek, Qwen and Kimi models (and gpt-oss). This is recorded in its approval's lineage. Before approving it for operational work, your organization's evaluation includes trigger sweeps with Canadian and defence context. Source: .planning/phases/74.1-model-passports-use-tiers-and-western-defaults/74.1-CONTEXT.md D-07. Controls: SA-11, SR-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g415; first milestone: Your organization's evaluation of Nemotron 3 includes trigger sweeps with Canadian and defence context (by 2027-06-30).
