## For exchange with allies {#coalition-exchange}

These matter when your organization exchanges labelled objects with allied partners. Here, an item that blocks production blocks live exchange with allies.

### Blocks production {#coalition-exchange-blocks}

- **G354. ZTDF conformance is not verified.** The exchange follows the public OpenTDF specification in a ZTDF-compatible profile. Checking it against ZTDF needs ACP-240 Edition A with its ZTDF specification, or sample objects from allies, and a test key access server (plan 45.2-10). Your organization requests them through its sponsor, and asks DND for ACP-240 Edition A with its ZTDF specification, which is still outstanding (owner action d). Until then exports are ZTDF-compatible, never called conformant. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-01. Controls: AC-16, AC-21. Owner role: shared. Planned in Phase 45.2.
- **G355. The Canadian DND/CAF label policy values are assumed, so operational exports that use them are refused.** Exports in the Government of Canada scales are labelled from the Canadian DND/CAF label policy profile (resources/label-profiles/can-dnd.label-profile.json). Its values are assumed from how DND security orders write markings: the policy identifier CAN and the classifications PROTECTED A, PROTECTED B, PROTECTED C, CONFIDENTIAL, SECRET and TOP SECRET, in an assumed order. The identifier's OID, the caveats, the releasability rules and a versioned policy information file are not known, so the OID is a placeholder set per target system and no OID is invented. An operational export always refuses the placeholder, and refuses the assumed values unless your organization's security officer records an exception for them; a trial export may use them and says so. Your organization asks the DND project technical authority for the target system's label-policy owner, who supplies the verified values (owner action a); each value is then replaced and marked verified. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-21 and D-22. Controls: AC-16, AC-21. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g355; first milestone: Exports are refused until the label values are in the signed policy (Phase 45.1).
- **G384. Signed NATO bindings use a provisional profile.** ADatP-5636 makes the signed binding mandatory, and its profile is in ADatP-4778.2 chapter 2, which your organization does not hold yet. Bindings are signed now with our own clearly marked provisional profile. Replace it when ADatP-4778.2 arrives. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-08. Controls: AC-16, SI-7. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g384; first milestone: The provisional profile is replaced when ADatP-4778.2 arrives (Phase 45.2).
- **G387. An export cannot be revoked once it is wrapped to a partner key.** Your organization runs no key access server for partners, so an export wrapped to a partner's key is final: nothing can withdraw access after release. Your organization's authorizing official accepts that risk, or a key access server at your site is planned. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-11. Controls: AC-21, SC-12. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g387; first milestone: Your organization's authorizing official accepts the risk, or a key access server is planned (by 2027-03-31).
- **G510. No allied test cell is arranged for the acceptance trial.** No allied test cell is arranged to check your organization's exports and partners' objects against an ally's own key access server and samples, so the exchange is checked only against the public OpenTDF quickstart, which proves wiring and never counts as acceptance. Your organization asks the DND project technical authority for an introduction to the Canadian Joint Warfare Centre (CJWC) experimentation and interoperability team, which runs the FMN trials and Project OLYMPUS (owner action a). The acceptance trial (plan 45.2-12) runs once the cell supplies a test key access server with its own samples. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-23 and the owner actions; 45.2-RESEARCH.md section 10 (T5). Controls: AC-16, AC-21, CA-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g510; first milestone: The CJWC experimentation and interoperability team, introduced by the DND project technical authority (owner action a), supplies a test key access server and its own samples; plan 45.2-12 then runs the acceptance trial (Phase 45.2).
- **G511. No vendor samples paired with a non-production key access server.** No vendor has supplied sample containers paired with a non-production key access server of its own, so the exchange cannot yet be checked against a second implementation; a sample paired with an unrelated key server does not count. Your organization asks Virtru's systems-integrator team or XQ Message for such samples (owner action c). The acceptance trial (plan 45.2-12) may use them in place of an allied test cell. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-23 and the owner actions; 45.2-RESEARCH.md section 10 (T5). Controls: AC-16, AC-21, CA-3. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g511; first milestone: Virtru's systems-integrator team or XQ Message supplies sample containers paired with its own non-production key access server (owner action c); plan 45.2-12 then runs the acceptance trial with them (Phase 45.2).
- **G512. Partners' signing certificates are checked without fetching revocation lists.** Partners' signing certificates on NATO bindings are checked against the trust anchors pinned for each partner in the signed policy, without fetching their certificate revocation lists, because the exchange never dereferences a URI from a partner's file. A partner's certificate is revoked here by your security officer removing that partner's anchor from the signed policy, which turns the partner's earlier arrivals back into not checked. The owner accepted this default on 2026-11-24. It is revisited if a partner or the authorizing official requires revocation lists to be fetched. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-08. Controls: AC-16, SC-12, IA-5(2). Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g512; first milestone: The owner accepted this default on 2026-11-24; it is revisited if a partner or the authorizing official requires revocation lists to be fetched (Phase 45.2).

### Does not block production {#coalition-exchange-does-not-block}

- **G353. The exchange receiving key is RSA-3072 because OpenBao has no ECDH.** OpenBao cannot do ECDH, so the key that opens objects sent to your organization is an RSA-3072 key held in OpenBao, not a P-256 key. It works with partners that use RSA key access. Revisit it when OpenBao adds ECDH or the exchange gains a post-quantum key access type. Controls: SC-12, SC-13. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g353; first milestone: Key access types are reviewed against the ACP-240 edition your organization receives (Phase 45.2).
- **G356. Partners without post-quantum support get classical key access only.** Partners have no post-quantum key type, so key access at the boundary is classical (RSA or P-256), which a future quantum computer could open from a recording. Each export records the key access algorithm, the export dialog says so, and your organization's security officer can set the highest level a partner may receive that way. The security officer accepts this condition for each partner. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-12 and D-13. Controls: SC-12, SC-13, AC-21. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g356; first milestone: Key access types are reviewed against the ACP-240 edition your organization receives (Phase 45.2).
- **G385. NATO policy value lists are needed only to write labels in NATO policy.** Writing a label in the NATO policy itself needs the value lists of AC/322-N(2011)0130-REV1. Exports label in your organization's national policy and the common partner policy, so the lists are needed only if your organization decides to write NATO policy labels. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-03. Controls: AC-16. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g385; first milestone: Your organization decides whether it writes labels in NATO policy (Phase 45.2).
- **G386. Whether the NATO schemas may be kept as test data is not answered.** No schema, prose or example from ADatP-4774 or 4778 enters the repository; the test vectors are our own. Whether the schemas may be kept as test data is a question to your organization's national security officer. Until it is answered they stay out of the repository. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-02. Controls: AC-16, SA-11. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g386; first milestone: The national security officer's answer is recorded (by 2027-03-31).
- **G455. RSA key access with partners' OpenTDF tools needs OAEP with SHA-1, which our receiving key cannot open.** The OpenTDF reference tools wrap a payload key for an RSA key with RSA-OAEP and SHA-1, while OpenBao Transit opens RSA only with OAEP and SHA-256. So an object a partner's stock OpenTDF tool addresses to your organization's receiving key exchange-receive-\<site\> cannot be opened, and an export to a partner's RSA key uses the hash the partner names, which for the OpenTDF reference server is SHA-1. Partners are asked for an EC key (ec:secp256r1) or SHA-256, and to address objects to their own key access server, which Phase 45.2 reaches through rewrap. Whether SHA-1 in OAEP padding is acceptable under ITSP.40.111 is not verified; your organization's security officer decides before any export uses it. Source: .planning/phases/45.1-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-labels-and-adapter/45.1-RESEARCH.md sections 1 and 5. Controls: SC-12, SC-13. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g455; first milestone: The development round trip with the OpenTDF quickstart's key access server and the acceptance trial with a partner settle which OAEP hash each partner uses (45.2-10, 45.2-12) (Phase 45.2).
- **G500. Labels on partner files that cannot be checked are confirmed by an exchange officer.** Partners whose systems are not like ours can send files whose label cannot be checked: a binding with no signature, a signature by an anchor your organization has not pinned for that partner, a form this version cannot check yet, a marking read from the file's text, or no label at all. Such files are held in quarantine in a protected cell at a provisional label, and an exchange officer confirms, raises or sets the label; a label lower than the sender's is refused. A person's confirmation is recorded as that person's act, never as a check of the file, so a mistaken confirmation is the risk that remains. Setting the label of an unlabelled arrival below its holding ceiling (the agreement's ceiling, released to no one) is not lowering: the holding label is your organization's protective default, not the sender's claim. Your organization's security officer accepts this condition; pinning each partner's signing anchors in exchangePartners turns claimed labels into checked ones. A label counts as checked only while the person who recorded the arrival is an exchange officer and the partner's anchor is still pinned, so removing an anchor turns that partner's earlier arrivals back into not checked. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-25, D-28 and D-29. Controls: AC-16, AC-21, SC-16. Owner role: owner. Tracked as POA&M item g500; first milestone: Plans 45.2-13, 45.2-16 and 45.2-07 hold every such file in quarantine for an exchange officer; the condition is reviewed with each partner's pinned anchors at the acceptance trial (45.2-12) (Phase 45.2).
- **G501. Partners' own national markings are not read yet.** Markings on plain files are read only when your organization's signed classification section lists them as patterns, through the marking reader of Phase 70.1, which only ever raises a label. Partners' national markings are read once your security officer adds them there as patterns mapped to your organization's labels; until then such files arrive unlabelled and an exchange officer labels them, and a site with no classification section reads no markings. Each partner's label-policy owner can supply its marking guide for the security officer to add. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-30. Controls: AC-16. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g501; first milestone: Each partner's marking guide is asked for at the acceptance trial (45.2-12, owner actions a and c), and its markings are added as classification section patterns (Phase 45.2).
- **G502. Partner key servers with 2048-bit RSA keys can be used only until the end of 2030.** ITSP.40.111 version 5 (section 5.1) asks for RSA keys of at least 3072 bits by the end of 2030. Partner key servers may use 2048-bit RSA keys today, because the public OpenTDF key access types name them, so from 2031-01-01 every export wrapped to a 2048-bit partner key is refused. Your organization's own receiving key is RSA-3072. Partners are asked for an EC key (ec:secp256r1) or a longer RSA key before then. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-32. Controls: SC-12, SC-13. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g502; first milestone: Plan 45.2-06 refuses exports wrapped to a 2048-bit RSA partner key from 2031-01-01 (Phase 45.2).
- **G503. Labelled mail and chat from partners are not read.** NATO profiles labelled mail (ADatP-4778.2 chapter 3, a binding object in a mail header beside the RFC 7444 security label header) and labelled chat (chapter 4, XMPP), and military mail gateways support them with S/MIME security labels. Your organization's exchange is a file handover at the release boundary, not a mail or chat gateway, so these labels are not read: a saved message arrives as a plain file and is held as unlabelled unless a marking your organization lists is found in it. A mail adapter is planned when a partner or the allied test cell shows it hands over labelled messages as files. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-33 and 45.2-RESEARCH.md section 12.3. Controls: AC-16, SC-16. Owner role: shared. Tracked as POA&M item g503; first milestone: Revisited with the partner's samples at the acceptance trial (45.2-12); a mail adapter is planned if a partner hands over labelled messages as files (Phase 45.2).
- **G504. Some OpenTDF forms are refused as not supported yet.** Some forms of OpenTDF objects are not read yet: NanoTDF, objects whose key is split across several key servers, remote key access, and post-quantum key access addressed to your organization's own key. Such objects are refused with a plain sentence; post-quantum key access addressed to a partner's listed key server opens through that server. Each form is added when a development or partner sample uses it. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-24. Controls: AC-16, SC-13. Owner role: maintainers. Tracked as POA&M item g504; first milestone: Revisited when the development round trip or a partner sample uses one of these forms (45.2-10, 45.2-12) (Phase 45.2).
